name: Faith
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a large, extra-secure garden to keep me safe as I learn about the home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Faith is a beautiful girl who came to us from a breeder and was initially incredibly shut down and terrified of people. She would run away from any human interaction and wouldn't even eat when people were around. However, Faith has made some incredible progress since arriving with us, and we are so proud of how far she has come. She is slowly learning that people can be kind and has built a lovely bond with someone she knows and trusts. She will now come over when called, and although she is still easily spooked, she is beginning to show us more and more of her sweet personality. Her walking has also improved, and she is now much happier exploring on her harness, although she will still need quiet walking areas where she isn't overwhelmed by too much going on around her.

Faith has also started to discover just how much fun life can be! She has begun playing with toys and chasing balls around our big yard, and it is wonderful to see her running around and enjoying all the space rather than sitting nervously in the corner. She recently had her first little experience in our onsite accommodation, where she spent a few hours with her kennel friend. We weren't sure how she would cope with this new environment, but she really surprised us. Although she was still a little worried by noises and would move around when she heard something unfamiliar, she eventually jumped up on the bed, curled herself into a little ball and settled down beside someone she knows. This was such a special moment for Faith and showed us just how much she is beginning to trust.

Faith absolutely adores other dogs and truly comes alive when joining her friends for playtime. She approaches them with a full-body wiggle and gains so much confidence from having them around. She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her continue building her confidence and show her the ropes of home life. As a Collie, she will also need plenty of enrichment and exercise to keep her busy once she has settled in.

Although Faith is doing brilliantly with people she knows, she is still extremely nervous around new faces and will need to be given plenty of time and space to build trust. She recently had a meeting with potential adopters, but found the experience too overwhelming and wasn't comfortable approaching them. Her adopters will need to understand that she won't be a dog who immediately comes over for a fuss or settles into family life straight away. She will need an adult-only home with Collie experience, where her progress will be celebrated and she can continue learning at her own pace. Faith has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient adopters who can help her with house training, lead walking and all the other new experiences that come with family life. She will also need an extra-secure garden of at least 6ft to keep her safe as she settles in.

Faith really is such a sweet girl who tries her very hardest to be brave, and the difference in her since she first arrived has been incredible. She has so much love to give once she feels safe with someone, and we know that the bond she builds with her forever family will be incredibly special. She will need someone who is willing to take things slowly, not expect too much too soon and give her the time and space she needs to find her paws. In return, we know there is a very loving little girl waiting to shine. We desperately hope someone will look past her initial nervousness and give this special girl the chance she deserves.

Faith has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

My little Faithy, the difference in her since she first arrived is incredible and I’m so proud of the progress she’s made and the bond she’s building with me.

She’ll now come to me when I call her over, she’s started to play with toys and chase balls down the big yard and she’s running around enjoying all the space down the big yard instead of sitting in the corner.

I took her in to the onsite accommodation for a few hours one evening to see how she would settle, she was with her kennel friend but I expected her to be restless and not settle but she exceeded my expectations. She did move at any little noise but she also jumped up on the fed curled in to a ball and just layed there with me. She did amazing and I’m so proud of her.

Faith is doing brilliant with me but with new people she is still extremely nervous and will keep her distance, she recently had a meet with potential adopters and she wouldn’t go near them, so if you pick Faith please be prepared to give her the time and space she needs but if you do that I promise you’ll get such a loving little girl in return.

Faiths walking is doing much better although she is still spooked by everything so she will need walks in quiet areas.

Faith arrived to us as an incredibly shut down, truly terrified 6 month old pup. She would run from me, frantic to get away from any human interaction. She wouldn’t eat whilst I was around & taking treats from me seemed like an unreachable milestone.In the last 2 months, Faith has progressed so incredibly well. She now walks on a harness, although is still easily spooked. She walks best with people she knows and has built trust with. She will take treats off me in her kennel & sometimes when she is walking on her harness providing it’s not too busy around her. Her favourite high value treat is definitely hot dogs & I found these were the way to her heart!Every day Faith joins a group of dogs for a big pack playgroup down our big yard. This has been instrumental to Faith’s progress and she truly adores other dogs & will approach them with a full body wiggle. She truly comes alive down the big play yard & it’s so nice to see her act like the puppy she is. She has learned how to play with toys too, although can’t be left unsupervised with soft toys. She enjoys them a bit too much!Down the big yard the other day, I slowly approached Faith to see if I could get near her in such an open space. As I approached Faith gave me a little tail wag & even allowed me to give her some gentle fuss. It might sound small but for a dog like Faith it’s huge. She would do anything to get away from human interaction before, yet now even with ample space & opportunity to run, she stayed for fuss instead.Whilst she is progressing well with us, kennels is simply not the right place for a puppy. We do our best for her of course but she is spending crucial developmental months in kennels instead of a home.She really is such a sweet girl who tries her very hardest to be brave, she just needs someone to see her progress already and recognise her potential. The 3 other collies Faith came in with have all been adopted and found their ‘forevers’, yet wait continues for our sweet angel Faith.

Faith has come into our care from a breeder and is now looking for a very special home where she can begin to discover how lovely life can be. She is a very nervous little girl who is feeling quite overwhelmed to find herself here. It is clear that she has had very little socialisation in her past, and she finds people very worrying at the moment. She isn't ready to approach us just yet, so her new family will need to be patient and allow her the time and space she needs to build her confidence.

Faith will need a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience of scared dogs and dogs of a similar breed. She will need people who understand that gaining her trust may take time and who will be happy to let her progress at her own pace, without any pressure or expectations. She takes great comfort from other dogs and relies on them for reassurance, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the way and become her friend.

Faith has never lived in a home before, so there will be lots of new things for her to discover. Her adopters will need to be very kind and understanding as she learns about home life, including all those everyday sights, sounds and experiences that many dogs take for granted. She will also need help with learning new skills such as house training. Faith doesn't yet know how to walk on a lead, so this will need to be introduced very gently, starting with practice in the safety of her home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Faith is going to need a very special family who can see past her worries and give her the time, patience and understanding she needs to blossom. We hope that, with the support of a lovely doggy friend and a family who will never ask too much of her too soon, she will gradually begin to feel safe and discover just how wonderful being someone's cherished little companion can be.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Tippins
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need another dog my size or larger in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk on lead but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have spent some time in a home, but still have lots to learn.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She can be apprehensive when meeting new people and may bark at strangers, but once she feels comfortable, her wonderful personality shines through. She has formed lovely bonds with staff at the rescue and, once attached to someone, she adores cuddles and wants to be as close to her favourite people as possible. She is a ridiculously affectionate girl who gives her whole heart to those she trusts.

Tippins was briefly adopted as an only dog, but has sadly returned to our care as she really struggled without another dog by her side. Although she didn't appear to rely on other dogs for comfort in kennels, she became very shut down in the home and struggled to come out of her shell. We therefore feel she will need a calm and confident resident dog, her size or larger, to act as a role model and help her settle. She isn't particularly cuddly with other dogs, but she shares her kennel well and we believe having another dog around will help her feel more secure while she adjusts to her new surroundings.

Tippins walks beautifully on her harness alongside her handler, although busy places and traffic can still make her nervous. Her new family should continue her confidence-building with quiet walks and plenty of reassurance.

Although she has spent some time in a home, Tippins had never experienced home life before her adoption and so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and house training. She will need a quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that settling into a home may take her some time. Once she feels secure, she will try her very best to be brave and become a devoted companion.

Tippins can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who are sensible and able to respect her need for a gentle introduction. Her adopters should also be prepared to welcome her onto the furniture, as we suspect this affectionate girl will thoroughly enjoy being close to her people once she feels safe.

Tippins has returned to us with an ear infection and is currently receiving treatment. Our vets are monitoring her ears and will continue to provide any treatment she needs. She will need her ears to be monitored and cared for in her new home as appropriate.

Tippins is a very special little lady who has made fantastic progress with us. With the right canine role model, an experienced and peaceful home, and the time she needs to settle, we hope she will finally discover just how wonderful life can be.

Tippins has been with me for more or less the whole time she’s been at the rescue and I honestly couldn’t love her anymore if I tried. Getting to spend time with her every day is an absolute privilege and I’m so grateful I get to look after her until she finds her forever home. She makes me laugh and smile every day and our cuddle sessions are my favourite thing in the whole world. I don’t think I’ve ever known a rescue dog to be as affectionate with me as she is. She literally just wants to be as close to me as possible at all times, and she also gives the best kisses!

Tippins can still be a little standoffish when she first meets new people, but at the rescue it doesn’t take her long to drop her guard with them. She did however struggle when she was briefly adopted. She was in the home for 3 weeks and sadly she just completely shut down. She hid in her safe place for the whole time and couldn’t find it in her to approach her new mum. She was adopted as an only dog, so we’re not sure if not being around another dog was the issue.

She’s not reliant on dogs at the rescue and she’s definitely more human focused, but because we don’t want a repeat of what happened last time, we are looking to home her with a resident dog. She can get a little jealous over attention, so a dog her size or larger would be the best fit. She’s never done anything and I do think she’ll be absolutely fine once she settles in and finds her feet, but it’s just something her future adopters should keep in mind!

Tippins walks perfectly to heal on a lead and also really, really enjoys her time in our secure yards. She loves to run around after me and frolic around without a care in the world. It’s lovely to see and it really gives me a glimpse of what her life could be like in her forever home. I hope she doesn’t have to wait much longer.

I’ve worked with a LOT of dogs over my 7 years of being at the rescue, and when I say this girl is really something special, I truly mean it. She’s a ray of sunshine on a cloudy day, a shoulder to cry on when you need it, and a breath of fresh air always. I adore everything about her and I will genuinely be very jealous of her future family.

She deserves to be absolutely cherished and doted on for the rest of her life, and loved unconditionally. Please don’t keep her waiting too long.

Tippins has been with me for about a month now, and I have really, REALLY fallen for her. Even though she presents as a nervous girl and will bark at strangers, it doesn’t take her long to let her guard down at all. When she does, she is your best friend, your shadow, your snuggle buddy... and you are her whole world. She absolutely adores the people she loves and really gives her whole heart to us. She is ridiculously affectionate, and I fear she’s so wasted being in kennels.

Tippins walks beautifully on a harness right by my side and looks up at me to check in constantly. She can still be nervous in busy places and around traffic, but that is something that she’ll get used to in time. I would recommend her adopters do some practice in the garden first before they venture out, and definitely establish a bond with her first.

Even though Tippins has never been in a home before, I’m pretty certain she’s going to want to join everyone on the furniture for snuggles, so this must be welcomed with open arms. Every day with me, she jumps up onto the bench next to me in the play yard, and she loves it when I sit in her bed in her kennel with her. So she’s a cuddler for sure!!

Please don’t keep this very special girl waiting for too much longer. She deserves to be loved and in a home so much.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a little apprehensive when she first meets new people, but she is already showing signs that her confidence is growing. Once she knows you, she enjoys a fuss and is happy to be handled. Tippins has a big personality and is a fun girl to spend time with.At the moment, Tippins is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with at least one other confident resident dog for support and companionship. She has always lived with bigger dogs and seems happiest around them. Tippins can be a little bossy with less confident dogs, so she wouldn't be suitable to live with smaller or younger dogs. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see if she could adapt to being an only dog. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience that can understand her needs.As Tippins has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she settles in and learns what home life is all about. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that can allow her time to settle into a calm environment.Tippins already walks on a lead, but doesn't seem to be overly confident on this so she will need continued support as she learns, and once she has settled into her new home, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog so that she can continue lead training.Tippins is a lovely girl with lots of character. She's already showing us what a sweet dog she is, and we hope that, with time and patience, she'll continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.Tippins is now receiving regular cleanings from the vets for waxy ears and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with one kind resident dog. I cannot live with cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk well on a lead and harness, and am doing well with those I trust.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Gail has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived, she was a very scared girl who found human interaction extremely overwhelming and would often hide away. Since then, she has made some really encouraging progress and is gradually learning to feel safe in her surroundings. She is still a cautious girl who enjoys having people nearby but prefers to have her own space rather than seeking lots of physical affection. She will allow gentle handling and is slowly learning to trust those around her.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle at her own pace. Gail is a sensitive little girl who can struggle with change, so she may take a step backwards initially when moving into a new home and will need plenty of patience and understanding.

Gail relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will be looking for a home with one kind, confident resident dog to be her friend. She is still learning how to share her space and can be a little sassy if other dogs get too close, so she would be happiest with a calm dog who understands her boundaries. Once she bonds with another dog, she really enjoys their company and takes confidence from having them around.

Gail has started going out for walks beyond the garden and is making progress on her lead in quiet areas, particularly when somewhere familiar. She is not yet ready for busier roads and will need her adopters to continue building her confidence gradually. Her housetraining is coming along well, with very few accidents, although she will still need time to adjust to the routines of a new home.

Shortly after Gail's arrival, she started showing signs of back pain, as well as some weakness and unsteadiness. As she is a Dachshund, she had x-rays to investigate possible spinal issues. These showed several mineralised discs in her spine but no obvious spinal cord compression. She was given pain relief and crate rest, and initially returned to activity with the help of a supportive back brace. Gail has made a good recovery and is currently doing well. She is also receiving red light therapy and Bowen therapy, wears a therapeutic magnetic collar and has continuous access to warmth to help keep her comfortable.

Gail's adopters will need to be aware that any future issues relating to her back would be classed as a pre-existing condition and would not be covered by insurance.

Gail is a truly special little girl who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She is still very much a work in progress, but with a quiet home, lots of patience and the reassurance of a kind canine companion, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

Gail has been making progress in foster and is gradually becoming more comfortable and starting to feel safe around the resident dogs. She is still a cautious girl who enjoys having people nearby but generally prefers to have her own space rather than seeking lots of physical affection. She is settled in the home, sleeps well and is happy to relax in her surroundings.

Gail gets on with other dogs but is still learning how to share her space and will let them know when she needs a little room. She is happiest around calm, respectful dogs who understand her boundaries.

She is becoming more confident with handling and will tolerate having her harness put on with a little patience and reassurance. She has also started going out for walks beyond the garden and is making progress in quiet areas, although she is not yet ready for busier roads. Her housetraining is coming along well, with very few accidents.

Gail is still very much a work in progress and will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand her needs and can give her the time and space to continue building her confidence. She has been receiving red light therapy and Bowen therapy, wears a therapeutic magnetic collar and has constant access to warmth to help keep her comfortable.

She is making progress at her own pace, and we hope that with the right home and continued support, she will continue to blossom.

What incredible progress this girl is making! I'm constantly impressed and surprised by her.I only work with Gail 1-2 times a month, and I'm always blown away by how far she's come when I see her again. Some things that may not seem like much can be huge milestones for our ex-breeding dogs - three months ago, Gail could only be touched by a few members of staff and was very anxious in human presence; six weeks ago, she would only tolerate having her harness put on and being walked by the two people she knew best; two weeks ago, she was walking with a few people but still spending most of her time in the back of her kennel hiding, and would try to hide in corners if she saw anyone unfamiliar; and today, she went on a 20 minute walk with me, then cuddled in my lap afterwards! She even goes for walks with volunteers she's never met before and is incredibly brave meeting new people. When visitors walk past, Gail runs to the front of her kennel with her tail wagging.Gail is a lovely little dog with so much personality. She's going to be the queen of wherever she ends up, and she deserves to be spoiled rotten! Hopefully, Gail's perfect home is right around the corner. Until then, we'll keep on showing her all the love and kindness we can.

We're super pleased with Gail's progress over the last few weeks.

Initially, we started yarding her with other dogs. She coped really well but would tell them off if they were too lively and in her face. We then started kenneling her with a female Cavalier, and she coped very well and seemed happier in herself. We then added a lively Poodle, but Gail told her off, so now she's just with the Cavalier. So, we've learnt that Gail can cope day and night with a calm dog, and on night duty, I saw them snuggled up in the same bed.Gail's walking is much better, but only with the staff who know her well. She follows her nose on a walk and likes walking in longer grass. Gail will roll over for a tummy rub but is still a little unsure about too much fuss.Gail is a happy little girl, full of character, who loves to carry her favourite toys around, and she's not possessive of them.

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Margate
description:
I need an experienced adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, though may be able to live with a calm female.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I can resource guard and will need adopters who can manage this.

I’m fully vaccinated and neutered. I have received treatment for an ear infection.

Margate has now spent over2 and a half years in kennels. That’sover 900 daysof waiting. Waiting while thousands of people have walked past his kennel. Waiting while his friends have come and gone. Waiting for someone to truly see him.

Everyone here adores Margate - he’s smart, affectionate, and bursting with personality. But love from staff isn’t the same as a forever home, and Margate is more than ready for his next chapter.

Since staying with us, Margate has received a dental treatment and had a cyst removed from his back left leg.

Margate came to us from a breeder in November 2023. He'sincredibly intelligent,loves a challenge, and will do absolutely anything for a tasty treat. He picks up tricks like lightning - he knows “sit”, “paw” and “speak” and he’s always ready to learn more. He thrives when his brain is engaged and would be an excellent candidate for scent work or activities like cani-cross (on-lead only!). He’s been described asone of the smartest dogs we’ve ever worked with.

He'svocal, a bit cheeky, and loves to tell us when it’s breakfast time - you can hear his excited barks all the way from the car park. He may come off as bouncy and bold, but beneath the surface, Margate is a sensitive soul who, sadly, has beenlet down by humans before. He can get worried easily, especially in overwhelming environments like the vet, where he becomes a bit of a puddle of anxiety (though he's muzzle-trained and manages with support).

Margate does require avery specific kind of home, and we won’t sugar-coat it - he’s not a “starter dog.” He needs:

Margate ispossessive around food, toys, and bedding, likely stemming from insecurity in his past. These behaviours are manageable - we’ll give guidance - but his adopters will need tounderstand and work with him, never punish or push him beyond his limits. Setting him up for success is the key.

Margate will test you - not because he's difficult, but because he's clever, spirited, and sensitive. But once you have his trust, you’ll havea bond that’s unbreakable.

Because Margate isn’t a dog you can bring home on a whim. He’s forsomeone extraordinary. Someone who sees past the behaviours and looks into his big, soulful eyes and says,“I’ve got you now.”

Margate has come so far during his time with us - he’s learned manners, made friends, gained confidence, and shown us theincredible potentialhe holds. But he deserves so much more than life in a kennel, no matter how much we love him.

Margate isnot for everyone, but if he’s for you - truly for you - then you are in for the mostrewarding journey. He’ll love you with his whole heart, and you’ll wonder how you ever lived without him.

If you think you could behis person, please don’t wait another day.

Margate’s forever is long overdue. Let’s not make him wait another year.

Margate will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

“My boy, Margate… I see all of you, and I’ll love you like you’re my own until your forever person comes along. I’ll be so jealous of whoever gets to share their life with you.”

If Margate’s profile wasn’t clear enough, I shall put it plainly. He is a superstar!

I have worked with Margate on and off for over a year. And I’d like to say he’s pretty fond of me, but nothing compares to the love he has for his main kennel mum. When I work on section with Margate, it’s a good day on the job. I show up early to greet him, and his excitement echoes through the section until he drags me to the yard to go potty. He has his morning zoomies before sitting on his pedestal, waiting for me to come into the yard for a cuddle and a fuss. His big brown eyes looking up at me as if to say, ‘I’ve missed you, dear friend. Thank you for joining me!’

We try our best to give him a good day, every day. He has his routine yard time where he enjoys his zoomies, barks at the birds and sniffs around looking for treasure (he knows he’s not allowed!). He says hello to the staff and visitors in reception and enjoys as many treats as he can get (Margate-approved ones only!). He has volunteers visiting him almost daily, and he really does appreciate every single one of them. Sometimes he enjoys social walks with other dogs, although he quite enjoys his one-on-one walks with the staff, too. It allows him to be treated like the superstar he is!

He also loves sitting on his pedestal, keeping an eye on everything happening around him and greeting visitors during the show rounds. But despite all the lovely people who come to see him, Margate is still waiting for his special someone to come along and give him the forever home he deserves.

Mr Margate (AKA Best Boy, the love of my life, Margherita Pizza, Maggie Moo, Margaret, and many other ridiculous nicknames) is approaching his third year here, and we're not letting a single day of his stay be wasted.

His days are full of so much love. So many people are part of Margate's family, and he adores seeing them all when he walks around the rescue or goes up to reception. He gets treats, but he's become quite fussy, so he'll only accept the best of the best.

He loves his long walks, his regular Margate-approved volunteers, his big yard time, sniffing as many sniffs as he can, and occasionally, he loves rolling in poo, which I am not so pleased about, but the boy enjoys it, so I don't judge.

He is the most super special boy who has so many adoring fans, and I am the founder of that fan club. I know his right home is out there; he just needs to wait a bit longer. But every single day here matters, and we're showing him all of the love, understanding, and support that we could possibly offer.

Mr Margate has utterly blown me away in recent times.Around a month ago, Margate had an unfortunate accident in the play yard, which lead to an emergency vet visit and his front paw needing stitches.

As one of the kennel managers, I see and interact with Margate regularly, but unfortunately I don’t get the luxury of working closely with him. But I think the story below highlights how much this beautiful boy wants to do the right thing.

I was the first person to get to Margate after his accident, do you know what he did when I got to the yard? He limped over to me, sat at my feet and cried out. I know some will say it’s anthropomorphism, but I am so sure in that moment, he was asking for help!

We had to carry Margate up to the top of the rescue to clean him off and assess his wounds, Margate is muzzle trained which meant we could safely assess his wounds without any risk - but honestly, he was SO well behaved. Yes he needed reassurance that he was, in-fact, being a good boy, but he blew me away with the trust he gave us.

We cleaned him up and quickly realised he needed to go for assessment with an out-of-hours vet. So, phone calls were made, and off he went, carried into a strange car and taken to a strange place and sedated for stitches… where again, he was such a good boy despite the pain he must have felt.

Upon return, poor Margate was on strict rest, with only short toilet walks, having bandage changes every few days, boots on and off for walks… his whole routine was turned upside down. Living in kennels, his world is already quite small, and these changes, although temporary and for his own good, made his world even smaller.

This is where Margate began to struggle a little; in pain and insecure, some of his guarding behaviours (which we haven’t seen for a long time) did resurface. Luckily, Margates main carer knows him inside & out, like the back of her hand, and created a plan for everyone to follow to help build his confidence back up. Just some small adjustments to keep him & everyone around him safe, which worked beautifully and we got to see the best of our boy again, despite still being on rest.

A few weeks have now passed, Margate has had his stitches out, his wound has healed beautifully - and he fully back to being our incredible, charismatic, clever, fun loving boy! It’s the highlight of my day to see Margate, he is so happy meeting everyone.

All of this is to say, Margate may not always be an “easy” dog, but he SO wants to do the right thing. Occasionally, his worries overwhelm him, but for someone with experience and patience, the love and joy you will receive in return will be so worth it.

Margate is, hand on heart, one of the most phenomenal dogs I’ve ever met, and after nearly nine years at Many Tears, I’ve met a lot of dogs! He is going to be someone’s absolute best friend and the most wonderful adventure companion.

His profile already covers all of his basic needs, so I won’t repeat those here, but I can honestly say that not a single day he’s spent in kennels has been wasted.

He has grown, learned, and loved so much during his time with us. His confidence has blossomed, he absolutely adores people, and he has made some lovely doggy playmates. He knows exactly which treats are his favourites, and he’s settled beautifully into his routine. He heads out to his yard at 9am, then off to reception to spend time with more people (and, of course, collect more treats!).

Throughout the day, different staff members make time to visit him for extra cuddles and attention, and he often spends my entire lunch break relaxing in the yard on sunny days. This is something he enjoys every second of.

Margate is such a genuinely lovely guy, which makes it all the more surprising that he’s had to wait so long. He has the sweetest nature and seems to want nothing more than to be everyone’s best friend. While he’s here, he’s made some great female play friends and absolutely loves spending time with them every day, soaking up the companionship and fun.

In one month's time Margate will have been waiting a full two years for his forever family to find him. He's been in our care for a full 23 months, that's around 700 days, he's never been adopted or gone to foster so he's not been returned to us, he just has been in the rescue for all that time, waiting.

The first picture is his original booking in photo, a very worried boy who arrived knowing nothing about what we would do for him and how much love he'd come to find in this place that should be a pit stop until their forever home is found. But he slowly grew to love people, he started to let his true personality shine through and he started to learn how to be the goodest boy in so many ways. We flash forward to today and I can still see his insecurities at times, these may never truly go away, but we help him through it all and he is one of the best dogs I have ever known.

I love him as I love my own adopted dogs and I try to let him have as much time and love as I can give him to help him not feel like a single day in kennels is wasted. Because this is two years of his life that he won't get back, so I damn well hope that I, and everyone else who has had a part in his journey, makes every single moment count!I know he'll always have his quirks and he does need a specific type of home with people who understand and can positively manage his guarding behaviours so that he doesn't feel the need to show these often. But he's such a good boy, he's so loved by all of us at the rescue, he's so smart and beautiful and funny and loving and such good company. I love every speckle of white he's grown on his face in these two years, I love every snuggle we have and every single moment he looks to me to let me know that everything is going to be okay.He needs the right home but more importantly, he deserves the right home, the right people. If I could move heaven and earth to give him his perfect life, I would.I do want him to leave the rescue, but only to people that can fully commit to keeping him safe and listening to every single guideline and boundary that we give them. One of which is that HE MUST be kept on a lead at all times when out of fully secure areas, his prey drive is very high and he deserves to be given everything he needs to be kept safe from being harmed, which means keeping him on a lead!I shall continue to love him with every day that he's in my care, as well as every day after he finds his perfect home and I wave him off.I'll be so happy that he was chosen but he's going to leave a huge hole in my heart. He's truly one in a billion.If you feel you may be the right fit, please read his profile completely and fill in a very detailed application form. We will be very particular about where he goes, because that is the least he deserves from us.My handsomest boy, Mr Margate

It's strange really, the bond you have with a dog on your section, especially if they're a long stayer.

They aren't your dog and yet you love them as though they are, you cuddle them and tell them how amazing they are, you pour your heart and soul in to them and try your very hardest to make each and every day special in some way because their time in kennels shouldn't be a waste or simply a means to an end.. it should matter and they should be living their life whilst waiting for a family of their own.

This is hard to do when there are so many dogs to care for, but you try to do the best for them and to make sure they know how truly special they are.

This is very much the case for my best friend, Margate (AKA Maggie, Margaret, Marjorie, Marge and he responds to all these names). He is the epitome of special, he does need a specific home with people who don't put him in bad situations, but when the right people come along, they'll be adopting a dog that will give them an absolutely smashing best mate and although I am desperate for his forever home to find him, the thought of saying goodbye to the most special boy with a heart the size of the moon and a brain that's double that still. I will feel as though I'm missing a huge chunk of my heart.

That's the job though, and in a strange way, that sadness is the most rewarding part. To be a part of finding them the perfect match that will not love them in spite of their quirks, but because of them. Someone who will choose them day in, day out with a certainty that just grows with every passing day. The love a dog shares with you, no matter for how brief or long, as many will know, stays in your heart forever.

I shall miss my best mate, Margate. His family will love him the longest, but I loved him first and I am so so grateful for that.

If you are interested in being the exceptionally lucky human that shares their life with this beautiful soul, then please read his profile and apply if you feel that you can give him all he needs.

Another day for Margate in kennels, after another week, another month... I'm just hoping that he doesn't have to wait until the another year mark.

Margate has been waiting for seventeen months for his ideal home to find him, that's 506 days in the same place, with people who adore him, but they're not just his people. He has to share his time with so many other dogs that are waiting for their forever homes, but none have been waiting as long as him.

He does require a special home, with people who can help him thrive and who will not fail him! But as long as they understand his needs and set him up for success, they'll get so much in return.

Margate needs a cat, child (resident and visiting) and small furry free home. He needs mental stimulation and he needs a good deal of exercise too, he is smart, so so soooo smart and this is where his humans will have to try and be smarter.

Margate learns everything very quickly and will need to have clear, set boundaries in his new home from the get-go. He will need to be given his own bed, that he learns is his bed and that he isn't allowed on the sofas or other furniture, especially to begin with. He will need a home that understands how to enrich his life, to use his brain and that LOVES a good walk. He could walk for miles. He could potentially do cani-cross as he loves to run, but Margate needs to be kept safe at all times, so he will need to be kept on a lead in anything he does (unless in a secure rented dog field area). He has a high prey drive and a nose that rivals the very best sniffer dog. If you had treats in your pocket at some point this year, he'll know.

The best set up for Margate would be a home that could adapt a room to be his area that is free of food and where he could go to sleep at night, if visitors came round or if you had to pop out to go shopping etc. He needs this to be his area that helps him feel safe and secure.

Although he can act like a big tough guy, underneath it all he is extremely sensitive and can get very worried by things.

How can we blame him for being this way? He's been let down by humans over and over again, he has had thousands of people walk by his kennel during his stay and no one chooses him.. I know that in a home that FULLY understands him and puts everything in place to set him up to succeed, then he will be the bestest boy you could ever wish to know. His heart is the size of the whole universe and he just needs someone to see him and commit to him, then they'll see what I see too. My boy, Margate, I see all of you and I'll love you like you're my own until your forever person comes along. I'll be so jealous of the person who gets to share their life with you.

Disclaimer - although he picks up agility things quite quickly, this is not something he should do to a competitive level as the environment of the events would not benefit him.

It is now over a year since Margate joined us here in Many Tears.  That’s 365 days of seeing the same kennel, and the same routine and watching his friends leave whilst he gets left behind. This year it’ll be the second Christmas in kennels and whilst others are snuggled up in a warm home and spoilt with presents, it’ll be another day in kennels for him.  Everyone here at the rescue loves Margate!

What can I say that already hasn’t been said about this wonderful boy ??

He’s a real character, smart and witty. Every morning I hear him from the staff car park and you know that he’s announcing breakfast time for the whole rescue!  At times he can be loud and bouncy but deep down he’s just a little baby who loves a good snuggle.

Margate really has improved over the year, learnt new tricks, muzzle trained, met loads of new friends and loves meeting new people! He’ll happily walk past volunteers and once instructed to sit and wait he will receive a fuss.

So far Margate has only needed the muzzle for the vets as a precaution, but he tends to turn into a puddle of mush as he’s actually quite scared of the vets.

Margate does have issues regarding high value treats, toys and beds. This is resolved by removing any food in the area, removing any toys from the yard before play time and using multiple blankets for bedding. This is something that can be discussed and helped with for potential adopters.

All Margate needs is for adopters to understand his requirement’s and who are willing to work with him in a home environment.  He is such a beautiful wonderful boy who really is wasted here in kennels?

Margate is still absolutely thriving and learning every day. He is such a clever boy who enjoys his training and the company of his kennel friend. He has come such a long way, but in a home he could truly excel as long as his new humans know how to keep his training progressing and his mind busy. I really hope he breaks free soon.

Margate is one of those dogs that once you know him, you fall head over heels in love with him. He is one of the smartest dogs I've ever worked with, picks things up incredibly quickly and tries very hard to please you. He would be the perfect only dog for someone who wants to pour lots of time in to training to build a strong bond with him and who will understand that he will train you if given a chance. He's a super special guy with so much love to give, he just needs the right person to choose him and fully commit.

Margate is a super cool bocker. He loves long walks and his time in the yard. He thrives with anything to get his brain working, so stimulation games are an excellent way of working Margate. The best way to work with him is definitely food, he will do anything for a tasty treat. Be careful though as Margate can be food possessive. As you can see by the pictures he is such an affectionate boy who loves a good fuss, to go with that he is just absolutely handsome! Margate has been in kennels for some time now and he does cope well with being in kennels, but he would just absolutely thrive in an active home with someone who is willing to keep him busy and stimulated. While he's been with us he's always had a female kennel friend but he would also be an excellent only dog, so you have the best of both worlds with Margate, but due to his exuberant nature he might grate on any resident dogs a bit . Margate is a stunning young man with bags of personality and he loves all the attention and will need an experienced owner as he is a rambunctious soul. Margate is an absolute star and deserves the best life possible, if you feel you can offer him his best life get in contact. Be sure to read all the previous updates on Margate also to get the best overall idea of this smart little man. This wonderful boy has been in kennels for far too long now and is ready to find his forever home and new loving family. Will you give him the chance to progress to the next chapter in his life?

Margate is a unique boy. Firstly, Margate will need an owner with some experience under their belt, to make sure his rehabilitation is successful. It is probably best that he is homed as an only dog, as Margate struggles to get along with some dogs due to his boisterous personality, which can be overwhelming. This doesn't mean he can't be homed with another dog, as he has had a few kennel friends at the rescue that he gets along great with, he just prefers human attention. Margate will not trust strangers 100% straight off the bat , he's always excited to see people and interact with them, but to build a bond of trust takes some time. However this is an experience that I've found extremely rewarding. I discovered this when I took him to the vets for an intimate checkup, and was surprised to discover that he would only allow me to carry out the checks. It absolutely melted my heart to know that he had complete faith in me. He really is a sweet, colourful personality with so much love and energy to give, he just needs some time, love and repetition with a regular owner to steer all that energy in a positive direction

Since his last update Margate has been enjoying learning tricks and enjoying fun little games. We have learnt to "sit" "paw" and to" speak". Margate enjoys his treats so was very keen to learn and being as smart as he is, picks up training in a flash. He is a very vocal boy and will bark until I give a treat. I do not give in and he will stop and wait patiently. Margate does need to learn manners so will need adopters to remind him of this and to show Margate right and wrong.

Margate has come on so well since being here and I must admit that I do have a soft spot for him. He enjoys his walks but does pull a little when he has found a sniff, but can easily be managed with lead training. I'm currently teaching Margate to sit when I stop walking, to get his pulling under control, and as Margate is food motivated, it’s easy to see that this can be managed with little trouble. He is already  getting the hang of it!

Margate does jump up on you and can jump quite high, so adopters will need to encourage Margate not to jump up, which I am currently showing him, but again he is a very smart boy who is eager to learn. He is a funny, friendly, and vocal boy who will needs adopters to be mindful of his needs and issues and redirect him properly for him to be the best boy he can. He is still kenneled with his friend who both still continue to share their bed and space together with no problems. He is still only young and I can't wait to see him flourish more than what kennel life can offer him. Please read Margate's profile and updates and see what an amazing boy he is. He is perfect for someone that loves to share an active lifestyle with their dog, and we can’t wait to see pictures of him on all his future adventures!

Margate is a gorgeous boy who I have spent a lot of time getting to know recently and has come along way since his last update. He greets you with a waggy tail and excitement when he knows you and does enjoy a gentle fuss. He is also getting used to his name and when you call him he will turn to you. Margate has very high energy and needs an active household who enjoys long walks and adventures and are able to stimulate him mentally as well as physically. He also walks on a lead but can pull, this can easily be managed with lead training and I believe will settle once he gets to go on regular adventures with his new family as he enjoys the sniffs of the world . Margate loves to learn and play and due to his breed, he will need adopters to understand the Bocker breed and the energy they have. Margate currently is kennelled with a female cocker and they spend their time together playing in the yard and rolling around in their beds together. They both get on very well!

Due to Margate's resource guarding, him and his kennel friend have bedding and blankets rather than plastic normal beds and they both share this with no problems. Margate does have food guarding issues  and is fed separately from his kennel friend. This can also be managed in a home with another dog if he is separated at feeding times. Margate does take treats from you when his kennel friend is present and has not shown any issues towards them but this still needs to be remembered. I have been visiting him when I'm not on the same section to issue treats around other dogs in proximity to get him used to being in the same space around other dogs with food and treats. With these small issues, Margate will need an adult home with no children.

Margate has mastered a few tricks with treats, learning to sit and give paw. He gets very excited when you ask him but need to tell him firmly. Margate can be jumpy and will jump on you so he will need a firm voice to encourage him manners. Margate learns quickly so I think teaching him house training, lead training as well as other tricks and manners will come quickly for him, especially with treats!

He is a stunning boy and overlooked here at the rescue. If you have a Bocker sized hole in your heart and are active, love long walks, adventures and fun. Please consider applying for Margate.

Hi! My name is Margate I am 2 years old male Bocker (Cocker X Beagle) and have found myself at this amazing place called Many Tears. When I first arrived, I was extremely worried with my new surroundings, and adapting back to kennel life was very tough. I have spent a little time in a home but because of my high energy levels and need for adventures my family wasn’t able to provide this so unfortunately through no fault of my own I have set out on an adventure to find my new forever home. In my new home I would need a child free home with no visiting children. In my new home I will need someone who understands my breed and have had experience with similar breeds. I am currently in a bedroom (Kennel) with a female Bocker called Nova. We don’t interact too much but we do enjoy one another’s company so I could be happy having another friend in my new home upon having a meet and greet at the rescue. I can also be an only dog as long as I have a loving owner who plays lots of games with me. I have mastered walking on a lead and I absolutely love to explore and go on walks so having a busy home who is as on the go as I am would really benefit my energy levels. I still struggle a little to find the toilet but if I’m shown I will definitely find a way to go in the right place. when I meet new people I can become a little shy and anxious so go slow with me, have a kind voice and I will wag my tail and ask you for some fuss. After spending a day with you i trust very easily and I will become your best friend. If you’d like to meet me I am currently at the many tears rescue.Margate is still waiting for his forever home at Many Tears and despite his struggles around food and resource guarding from humans and dogs when food is involved, all he needs is an experienced home with the ability to adapt and help Margate with this. He will bring so much joy into your home and he can't wait to be a cherished member of the family where he can go on lots of adventures and finally be loved.

Margate is a stunning but very confused boy who is overwhelmed to be here and has been through so much change recently. He has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. Initially when you first meet him he is mistrustful of strangers and unsure about being handled - he will make his worries known by growling. However once you have spent a few minutes in his company showing that you are safe he quickly warms up to you and jumps all over you for love and attention. We suspect he may have lived in a home before and then returned to the breeder hence his being unsure of people initially which is fair enough, poor boy! Margate already walks on a lead and would probably prefer to be an only dog.  Margate will need a cat free home as he is far too interested in them and a home without children or visiting children as he would find them too much. Margate may need help learning to live in a home and being taught housetraining skills. Margate is such a poor soul who just wants to be loved and to feel safe. Margate would need a home that is experienced in resource guarding and can help Margate work through his struggles. Margate can resource guard when he has food or high value treats/chews/bones around both dogs and people so this would need to be managed with an environment set up to ensure lovely Margate is set up for success.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sixpence
description:
I will need an adult only home, that will let me settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. We have now learnt that she is trying so hard to be brave and, although she is still quite nervous, we are seeing little bits of her cheeky Daxi personality coming through every day.

Sixpence seems to have had very little positive touch or affection before coming to us. She has recently moved in to foster and is happy to take treats from her foster parents but is not quite sure about being stroked yet. She will allow them to put her harness on as long as she is in a quiet corner and things are taken slowly. You can tell she isn't entirely comfortable, but she trusts us enough to allow it and is always very happy to enjoy a little cheese reward afterwards! With continued positive reinforcement, we are confident that this will improve as Sixpence learns that good things can come from new experiences.

Sixpencerelies heavily on other dogs and really enjoys being around her resident dog friends. She watches what they do and follows their lead for confidence, and she has even learnt from them how to use the dog steps to get onto the sofa and watch the world go by from the front window! She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she continues to find her confidence and learn about home life.

Penny is also discovering all sorts of things that she enjoys. She loves sunbathing, having the freedom to explore a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and, of course, cheese! She has a crate set up with a fluffy bed where she can go when she wants some quiet time to herself, and she seems to really enjoy having this safe space available to her.

Sixpence will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have breed experience and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and encouragement as she settles in. Her ideal home would have one or more small, friendly dog companions who can help her feel secure. We feel that children would be too overwhelming for Penny, so she will need an adult-only home.

Penny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she continues to learn about home life, including house training. She will also need to continue her harness and lead training at her own pace, as these are still very new experiences for her.

Sixpence is a very sweet little girl who is trying her very best to be brave. She has already made some lovely progress in the short time she has been with us, and we can't wait to see just how much more of her personality comes out as her confidence grows. She just needs someone willing to give her the time, space and love she needs to discover how wonderful her new life can be.

Sixpence has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Maddox, on behalf of Jesus Christ

We have had Sixpence or 'Penny' as she is known here for a little over a week. it is clear that she has had very little positive touch or affection before and she is trying desperately to be brave!

Although she is still quite nervous were are noticing her trying or learning something new everyday and her cheeky little Daxi personality is starting to shine. She has discovered a love for sunbathing, the freedom of a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and cheese!

Penny is happy to take treats from us but isn't currently sure on being stroked. We can put a harness on her as long as we find a quiet corner and go slow. you can tell she isn't entirely comfortable but let's us do it and enjoys her cheese reward afterwards. We have every confidence that this will improve with more positive reinforcement and learning just how amazing walks are.

She really enjoys being around her resident dog friends and follows what they do for confidence. She's even learnt from them how to get up onto the sofas with the dog steps and watch the world go by out of the front window. We have a crate set up in our dining room with a fluffy bed in for when she wants some time to herself which she likes.

Penny's ideal home would be a quiet one with one or more small dog friends and owners that are willing to give this girl the time and space she needs to learn her new life at her own pace. Sadly we think she would find children too overwhelming. We can't wait to see her confidence grow in her new life.

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. She will need time, patience and plenty of trust-building before she feels confident enough to come out of her shell.

Sixpence relies heavily on other dogs and will follow their lead, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about home life and finds her paws. She will need a calm and quiet home, with adopters who have breed experience and can understand her needs.

Sixpence has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns about house training. She is working with her kennel mummy on harness training and would like to continue this in her new home. She can live with sensible, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who will give her the time and space she needs. Sixpence is a very sweet girl who just needs someone willing to give her the chance to blossom.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about lead walking yet. A garden is fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and can still find people and handling very frightening. However, she has made lovely progress since arriving and is showing us more of her cheeky personality every day.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence. While she is still very worried about being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will sit close by while waiting for more. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know how she is feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. It is wonderful to see her becoming more comfortable in her surroundings.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she settles into family life.

Louise can be vocal around food and may give a warning growl, but she does not actually do anything and this appears to simply be her way of communicating that she would like some space. She can happily be fed alongside her canine friends as long as each dog has their own bowl and they stick to their own food. She is also absolutely fine taking treats, so this is something her adopters should continue to manage calmly and sensibly.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. This is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, but she has never tried to bite during these sessions. With time and patience, we hope she will continue to learn that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready for harness training, so her future family will need to carefully plan how and when to introduce this once she feels more secure. Everything must happen at Louise's pace so that she can continue building confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

My darling girl Louise (or Weezy as I call her) has been at the rescue for such a long time now and I really am desperate to find her the perfect forever home. She’s still taking baby steps with her confidence, but I truly think she’ll do so much better outside of a busy kennel environment.

One thing I’ve been working on more with Weezy is grooming. In my last update I wrote that she didn’t want to sit on the grooming table so I had to hold her on my lap, but she has since been brave enough to lay down and stay still for me to brush her. She does still have moments of panic and I have to gently scoop her up and reassure her to calm her down, and then she does recover quite quickly. Having treats is massively helpful as it distracts her from being on the table and being brushed. We still have a way to go, but she has gotten so much better.Even though she is still nervous and very sensitive, I am going to start harness training with her very soon. I think she will struggle with having something on her body at first, but I’m hoping she will get used to it. I’ll take it very slow with her and try to ease her into it as best I can. Wish us luck!

For such a small girl, she has a real big personality, and I just love her for it. She’s sassy, cheeky and chopsy and she puts a smile on my face every day.

Weezy’s favourite things:- Food!!! She is ridiculously foodie and will happily sit right next to me and wait patiently for some tasty treats. She also absolutely loves having chews.- Toys! Especially hard ones like Nylabones. I put toys in her kennel every day and she likes to pick them up and take them into bed to chew on. I often walk past and see her happily chewing away without a care in the world which is so lovely to see.- A cosy bed. No explanation needed .. she just loves being comfortable!

Weezy’s dislikes:- Dogs that are too over the top or in her face. She gets very overwhelmed by them and will run away.- Being touched and picked up. She’s a LOT better than she used to be, but she is still sensitive about it and doesn’t enjoy it.- Sharing food with her friends!!! She’s a real Joey!

Please don’t keep her waiting for too much longer!!

Louise has been with us for about 3 months now and even though she has progressed since she first arrived, things are happening very slowly and steadily. I would have liked for her to have gained more confidence by this point, but some dogs struggle with being in such a busy kennel environment to let their guard down … and Louise is one of them! That’s okay though. Making sure she’s happy and content within herself is the most important thing, and I’d say she is!

I haven’t really pushed Louise too far out of her comfort zone up until now, just because I didn’t want to send her backwards with her progress, but there does come a point where you have to, to prove to them that it’s okay. So today I took Louise into my grooming room for a very gentle and calm brushing session. She didn’t want to stand on the grooming table and kept clambering back onto me - which is the first time she’s ever done that - so I opted to keep her on my lap while I brushed her. She was settled for the most part, but she did have a little panic when we got to her ears as she had a couple of tangles which must have hurt her. I managed to cut them out with a scissors and then she was okay with me brushing around that area. I kept the session very short and sweet as I didn’t want to push too far, and I think it was the right decision. When I took her back to the kennel she didn’t sprint away from me or anything like that, so I’d say our relationship is still there!

Louise is such a special little character, and I really hope someone will see her in the same way I do soon. She deserves a life outside of kennels, one where she can finally start to thrive.

Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

name: Enfys
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

22-10-26 Enfys is the most wonderful girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. Shortly after Enfys arrived with us, we discovered she was pregnant and she soon gave birth to one puppy. She has been the most wonderful mum to little Eddie and now that he is old enough to find his forever home, Enfys is ready to start looking for her family too.

When she first arrived she was quite a worried girl, but she has settled in well and has really started to come out of her shell. She now absolutely adores the staff members who she knows well, but is still quite worried when meeting new people or experiencing new places, which is understandable.

Enfys is such a funny character, her favourite thing in the world is to roll over onto her back, which has been affectionately called her "diva downs" by those who know her! She loves to do zoomies around the play yard in the mornings while she waits for her breakfast to be prepared! We think with time, love and care she is going to blossom into the most wonderful girl.

Enfys can be quite worried, but can be an only dog in her home, with adopters who are able to offer her plenty of attention and time. However, she can live with another chilled dog who doesn't mind that she can be protective of her toys and will allow her to create her own safe space. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will help her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+.

Enfys has never lived in a home before so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has learned all about walking on a lead and harness while being with us and walks well although can be unsure in new surroundings, so will need more practice to gain confidence.

Enfys is a lovely girl who is already showing us little flashes of her personality. She has so much potential, and we know that with the right experienced home, she will continue to blossom.

Our vet has noted that she has a Grade 1 patella luxation in her right hind leg, which will need to be monitored although may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. She has been treated for a skin rash and has some areas of alopecia. She also has a smore mass inside her mouith which our vet says appears non-invasive and non-destructive, consistent with an epulis.
