name: River
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, but I have lived with another dog. See more below.

I would like a secure garden in a quiet area.

I can walk well on a lead and would like an active home.

I need experienced adopters to work on my reactivity with me.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

River originally came into our care in 2020 from a breeder and was adopted into a loving home. Sadly, her family later found they were unable to continue meeting her needs, and River has now returned to us.

River is a highly intelligent, affectionate girl who forms very strong bonds with her people. According to her previous home, once she feels safe she is extremely loving, enjoys close contact and seeks reassurance from those she trusts. She loves cuddles, gentle scratches, and being near her humans, and is very in tune with their emotions, often offering comfort when someone is feeling down.

River is a clever and enthusiastic learner who already knows a wide range of cues and enjoys training, enrichment and mental stimulation. She loves her toys, especially balls and tug toys, enjoys scent games such as “find it”, and is very food-motivated, peanut butter is her absolute favourite! She settles well at home, enjoys routine and structure, and is clean and non-destructive.

River enjoys her walks and would suit an active home with access to quieter walking routes. She walks nicely on a halti and enjoys being out and about, but can find busy environments overwhelming and may be reactive to dogs, vans or motorbikes when anxious. She will need confident handling and continued training, and should remain on lead unless in a secure area.

Although affectionate and loving, River is a sensitive dog and can struggle with unfamiliar people, visitors and loud or sudden noises such as fireworks. When frightened she may bark or retreat. For this reason, River is looking for acalm, quiet, adult-only homewithvery few visitors, ideally in arural or semi-rural setting. Her adopters must beexperienced with reactive dogs, patient, and willing to work at her pace while respecting her boundaries.

We are advised that River can occasionally display guarding behaviours towards her trusted humans, such as growling if another person enters the room while she is settled. This will need calm, confident and experienced management.

River is currently looking for a home as anonly dog, although she has previously lived with another small dog and may be able to live with a calm companion following careful introductions.

River may not be suited to everyone, but for the right home she will be an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion who has so much love to give.

A bit about River from her previous home:

Riverwill need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

I’m a staff member who hasn’t really worked directly with River. But we have a mutual understanding that I’m a friendly person who’s got treats… that’s about as far as my friendship with River has gone, until now.

However, I’d say she’s warming to the idea of me being a good friend. I get a bum wiggle and tail wag when she sees me now, and I get a paw in exchange for some tasty treats… a few fewer grumbles over the last few weeks.

Recently, I also had time to take River for a walk, an honour, as she’s very stranger-danger and has only a handful of staff members that she is a big baby around.

Now, the weather wasn’t great for said walk, and she definitely used her body weight to get more treats out of me. I happily obliged, as by the end of our short walk, River nuzzled me! She sat beside me looking for a head scratch and even sat in front of me, keeping a lookout while we waited for her kennel mum to come and get her.

You may think, ‘Why is the staff member so happy?’

Because River is a dog with boundaries and is not the typical dog that you see in a café or busy environment, just enjoying the scenery. She is reluctant to socialise with new people and prefers to keep her circle small and her environment on the quiet side. So, to even be willing to go for a walk with a staff member that she doesn’t socialise with often is a huge achievement for River.

If I had the right lifestyle for her, I’d 100% have her living the antisocial life with me, but I have hope that River is just waiting for the right home to see and appreciate her and all the quirks that just make her the most amazing dog you ever get to meet.

River is honestly the sweetest girl once she knows and trusts you.

Recently, I’ve been taking River around our reception area and spending some quiet time with her, helping her learn that people she doesn’t know don’t have to be scary.

River is now happily taking treats from numerous members of staff she doesn’t know, something that might seem so small to some, but for River and everyone who knows her it’s a massive achievement!!

Once River lets you into her world and that special bond is built, she will be your best friend for life. She has so much love to give; she just needs someone willing to take the time to earn it!

I really, really hope River’s people find her soon. It’s heart breaking to see such a loving girl waiting in kennels when I know just how much happiness she could bring to someone’s life.

River may need a little time to trust you, but i can promise you, she will be worth every second.

River and I have a complicated relationship. I have worked with river more or less since she came in to us. She seemed to have forgotten this fact and decided I was no longer a trusted person. To combat this, I decided to work closely with her to see if I could change her mind.One thing I learnt about river early on is that she loves a walk! So, naturally, I put her harness and muzzle on and took her for a 30 minute walk. She enjoyed this very much so! The next day, I took her out on a longer walk, around an hour. River will not get tired. She is happy to walk for days and happier still if you take her for so long. On one of our walks, we stopped by a church, had some cuddles and did some tricks. She’s very clever.

Another activity I did with her was taking her to our big sand yard (a large enclosed field), letting her roam free and playing fetch. Great for exercise, mental stimulation and, in turn, trust building. She loves to fetch, definitely one way to get a higher standing in her good books.As well as this, I spend a lot of time with her in her kennel, just trying to show her I’m a trustworthy human.

In conclusion, we now have a much better relationship. It goes to show; things that seem small actually make a big difference. River is an extremely clever, beautiful girl. She does not warm to everyone but, with time, patience and perseverance to break through to her, she will be your best friend. Ideally, she requires a home with no other dogs, a human who can spend the majority of their time with her, take her out and give her the stimulation she needs.

Just wanted to share quick update for our wonderful River! Her kennel mum has been working on showing River that visiting the vets isn’t always a scary ordeal. Today, I popped in with her to see how it was going. I was SO impressed!

Although she was hesitant to come in, once in the vets she settled enough to have the biggest cuddles (River gives the BEST cuddles). We spent 5 minutes or so telling her how beautiful and amazing she is and made sure to head out before she got too worried.

River is honestly one of those special, once in a lifetime dogs. Once she bonds with you, she has this incredible ability to make you feel like the most important person in the world. She gives you her whole heart. Whoever adopts her will be so lucky to have her in their life!

Our gorgeous girl River is still on the search for a new home and family and hopefully her forever one. River is continuing to do very well here at the rescue and has progressed so much since being back with us.

Having lived in a home River knows a lot of commands and has been very well taught. She's clean in her kennel and isn't destructive at all. Although, she has lived in a home before she does still struggle at times with busy environments and people she doesn't know. When shes greeted by someone she doesn't know she will bark out of uncertainty but if you offer her a treat she tends to make friends with you pretty quickly. There were only a couple of people who could work with River initially when she came back to us due to her being so overwhelmed and worried but now half the rescue can work with her so shes made massive progress and I couldn't be any prouder of her.

She walks lovely on the lead and absolute loves going out for walks or down the big yard where she also loves to play fetch. We have been training River to understand that going to the vets isn't all that scary. We have been desensitising her by walking her up the vet steps and just sitting there for a moment praising her. Before, she wouldn't even go up the steps so for her to do this and sit there for a moment is massive for her. Our next step will be to open the vets door and go from there. River is such a special girl and when she trusts you she loves you with her whole heart and she genuinely does make you feel so loved. Being Rivers Kennel Mum is honestly the best and having all that love and affection from her is just utterly amazing.

River is continuing to do incredibly well here and is trusting more and more people she meets each day. It’s been lovely to see her confidence grow as she builds good relationships with other people. As part of her ongoing desensitisation, we’ve been walking River around the front of the rescue and gradually up towards the vets. This helps her learn that these environments are safe and nothing to worry about. Throughout this training we give her plenty of praise and tasty treats, and she is responding really well.

Considering everything she’s working through, she’s doing brilliantly. River is muzzle and Halti trained, as she can be reactive to certain dogs and can be strong when she first heads out on walks. We are working on her reactivity daily, and she is improving.

Her future adopters will need to continue with this training to help her keep progressing and feeling secure. River is an absolute darling. She has such a loving nature and truly makes you feel so loved when you spend time with her. With the right support and understanding, she would make a wonderful companion and a very special addition to the right home

River is a gentle girl who has previously lived in a home and is already kennel clean, giving her a great foundation for her next chapter. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but with time and patience, she soon shows her sweet, affectionate side. Once she trusts you, River forms a lovely bond and just wants to be close to her people. She’s looking for a kind, understanding home that will give her the reassurance and love she deserves.

22-11-26 Angel is an inquisitive but timid lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is desperate to be brave and, although she is still a little unsure of us, she showed us that there is a lovely, curious girl hiding beneath those nerves. She is now happy to approach us and although does get a little shy she seems to enjoy some gentle tickles. Her tail was even wagging for her photos, which was lovely to see! We think that with a little time and reassurance, Angel will soon begin to blossom and show us more of her personality.

Angel would be best suited to a calm home with adopters who have experience of worried ex-breeding dogs and who have plenty of time to spend with her as she settles in to her new life. We would consider homing her with dog savvy children 9+. She will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep her safe as she has been known to climb.

Angel gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Angel has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, walking on a lead and harness and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding, allowing her to take things at her own pace as she gets used to her new surroundings.

Angel has already shown us that she wants to be brave, and we think it will be a wonderful thing to watch her confidence grow. With love, patience and a friendly canine companion by her side, she has every chance of becoming a happy and cherished little member of the family.

name: Milo
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I will need to be the only dog in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on a lead but will need my adopters to be understanding of my needs!

I have lived in a home before so may I may already know the basics.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home!

06-10-26 Milo is a super sweet boy who has come to us from a home through no fault of his own. Sadly, he has already been through more changes than a young dog should have to, and he is understandably a little worried in new environments. He takes a lot of comfort from people he knows, but once he feels comfortable, his fun and affectionate personality really starts to shine.

Milo is an incredibly sweet boy who absolutely loves being close to his people and thinks he is the perfect lap dog! He is happiest when he can have a cuddle and will happily climb up for a lap sit. He is a sensitive little soul and will need a kind and patient home where he can continue to build his confidence and learn that he is safe and secure.

Milo will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog and get all the fuss and attention for himself. We are told that he has had a previous incident with a cat and so he cannot be homed with cats or small furries and must be kept on lead unless in a secure area.

Milo has missed out on some socialisation, but he is currently working on his social skills and is making lovely progress. He can happily walk alongside calm dogs and has had some nice greetings. He doesn't always know what to make of other dogs yet and can sometimes get a little carried away when mixing, but with continued positive socialisation we are sure his confidence will grow. He can also react if another dog barks at him first while on lead, so his new family will need to understand this and help him learn how to navigate these situations.

Milo will need an adult-only home with people who have experience of bull breeds and understand what sensitive souls they can be.Although he is a wonderful boy, he would not be suitable for a first time dog owner.He will need a kind and patient family who can give him time to settle and continue building his confidence. He will also need the time he is left home alone built up gradually as he settles into his new home.

Milo will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep him safe, as he is a young and active boy who could be an escape artist if given the opportunity.

Milo is such a lovely young boy who has already been through so much change. With the right family, patience and continued socialisation, we know he will make a wonderful companion and be the loving, fun little lap dog he is so desperate to be.

name: Benji
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to have fun playtimes in.

I walk on a lead and would enjoy a nice walk once a day.

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

03-11-26 Benji is a beautiful, playful boy who originally came into our care as an unclaimed dog in 2024. He was adopted but has sadly returned to us because of illness in the family, meaning his owners were no longer able to care for him.

Benji is feeling a little out of sorts being back in kennels but is coping well. He is a super-loving boy who absolutely adores attention, cuddles and bum scratches. He has been spending lots of time in the office with us while his exercise is restricted and is always happy to soak up some fuss. He has lots of character and a wonderfully silly personality, and we know he would love nothing more than to be back in a home where he can relax on the sofa and enjoy life with his favourite people!

Benji can be a little reactive towards other dogs when out on walks, but having spent time in a home, he has made some lovely improvements. He is currently kennelled with a friend and we feel he could potentially live with another suitable dog or as an only dog. His adopters will need to be understanding of his needs and willing to continue supporting him with his training around other dogs. When Benji was initially with us, he could snap at feet when leaving his kennel, but this behaviour has improved massively since his time in a home. He is generally much better around doorways, although he can still become uncomfortable if someone lingers in a doorway or enters without greeting him, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this.

Having lived in a home before, Benji is familiar with the sights and sounds of everyday life and will hopefully settle back into a home routine with a little time. He needs a calm, adult-only home with adopters who understand his breed.

Benji was castrated and had nasal wedge surgery in 2024. He can still experience episodes of being sick, particularly following exercise, excitement or periods of stress. He is currently being trialled on a course of medication to see whether this helps manage his symptoms, but he may require further investigation and potentially additional surgery to address his breathing, such as BOAS surgery, in the future. His exercise and activity levels are currently being managed, so he will need adopters who are happy to accommodate his reduced exercise needs and understand that he may require further veterinary treatment and monitoring as needed.

Benji really is a lovely little man who is full of character and has so much love to give. He is a typical silly Frenchie who is desperate to get back to being the couch potato he deserves to be! With a calm home, understanding adopters and plenty of cuddles, we know he will be so happy to have a sofa to call his own again.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Fanta
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand I need space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-10-26 Fanta is quite a scared girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is in need of lots of TLC and the reassurance of a confident resident dog to help her feel safe. Fanta can be a little panicky and flighty, so she will need a very secure garden with high fencing to keep her safe while she settles into her new surroundings.

Although Fanta was shaking, she allowed us to pick her up and give her a gentle fuss to reassure her that we are here to help. She is still very unsure at the moment, so her new family will need to be patient and allow her the time she needs to learn to trust.

Fanta will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, as this will be a much-needed support system for her. A reassuring canine companion can help guide her and give her the confidence she needs as she settles in and begins to find her paws.

As Fanta has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to understand that this may take time and be prepared to let her progress at her own pace. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand she needs time to settle in. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience to better understand her needs.

Fanta is a very worried little girl, but she has already shown us that she can accept gentle affection even when she is feeling frightened. We hope that with a confident canine companion, a calm environment and lots of patience, she will gradually begin to feel safe and discover the happy new life she deserves.

Fanta has been given the Gift of Life by Aimee Helme

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

20-11-26 Lady is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is still finding her paws. She can be anxious and will need a little time and patience as she continues to build her confidence and settle into her new surroundings.

Lady will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance as she learns about home life. As Lady has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about house training and the other basics of home life. Walking on a lead may be a little overwhelming at first, so some gentle garden adventures and sniffs will be a good place to start.

She will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand her needs. Lady could live with older, sensible and dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who will respect her space and allow her to settle at her own pace.

Lady is a lovely girl who just needs a little understanding and the chance to discover how wonderful life in a home can be.

name: Blake
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I can walk on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will need a grain free diet & I have small ear canals!

06-11-26 Blake is a wonderful, confident boy who has come into our care from a breeder and is absolutely full of beans! He is your typical happy and excitable Staffy who loves everyone he meets and is always ready to make a new friend.

Blake is confident enough that he would be happy to be homed as an only dog as long as his adopter had plenty of time to spend with him, but he does get along really well with other dogs and could be homed with a kind resident dog who won't mind his enthusiastic personality. We would consider homing him with dog savvy teenagers aged 13+ and he would be best suited to a home with adopters who have dog experience.

Blake has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns all about home life, including house training. He will need a home with no cats or small furries.

He can walk on a lead and would love to find an active home with adopters who can keep him busy, enjoy adventures with him and understand his bouncy nature. Blake has already been showing us just how clever he can be and has recently learned to play fetch, even bringing the ball back! He even already knows how to sit on command. He is an eager-to-please boy with so much love and enthusiasm for life, and he is more than ready to find a family of his own.

We have been told the breeder that Blake requires a grain free diet, so this will need to continue in his new home. Our vet has noticed that he has narrow ear canals, but this does not seem to bother him.

name: Bramble
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I would like to be the only dog in my new home and cannot live with cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I walk well on a lead and I would love to go on plenty of adventures!

I have lived in a home before so I may already know the basics.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

05-11-26 Bramble is a very sweet lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was adopted for a short period but sadly returned due to her reactivity with other dogs. She absolutely adores people, but she can find seeing other dogs out on walks quite overwhelming, and her reactivity stems from fear rather than anything else.

She is currently working really hard on building positive associations with other dogs and is making some lovely progress. We have found several calm dogs she is happy to walk alongside, which is a fantastic step forward! Bramble is also being muzzle trained so her future adopters can continue this training and help her feel safe when out and about, particularly in busier areas.

Bramble is looking to be the only dog in her new home, where she can have all the attention to herself without the worry of sharing her space. She can live with older, sensible and dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand her needs. She will need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft, as well as adopters with previous experience of reactive dogs, her breed and ex-breeding dogs.

Bramble really is a lovely girl who is trying so hard to overcome her worries, and she has so much potential. She will need a family who understands that progress takes time, is happy to continue her training and can give her the patience and reassurance she deserves. We know that with the right people beside her, this special lady has so much to offer!

description:

Patoots takes comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance as she settles in and learns about home life. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

name: Pippa
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden to keep me safe.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Pippa is a very scared and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very worried about being handled and becomes stressed if we attempt to pick her up. She will try to jump from our arms and, because of this, we would consider her a flight risk and she will need fencing of at least 6ft in her new garden to keep her safe. She will need very careful handling and adopters who understand just how frightened she is at the moment.

Pippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Pippa has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and give her time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.

Pippa will need a quiet, confident, adult-only home where she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand her nervous nature and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Pippa is a very worried girl right now, but with the security of a kind canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe and gain the confidence she needs to enjoy her new life.

Pippa has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Rizzle
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she arrived she was quite overwhelmed and in need of plenty of TLC, but she has since started to come out of her shell.

Rizzle has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in and starting to learn about home life for the first time ever. She is making gentle progress and is even starting to wag her tail when her fosterer speaks to her and has ventured onto the sofa twice so far, although she is understandably still quite nervous and isn't yet feeling brave enough to approach but is trying her hardest to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place.

She has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training, though she is starting to get to grips with this already. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness as she is quite worried about being handled, but hopefully this will be introduced to her in the near future.

She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Rizzle has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Rizzle is a real sweetheart, but still very nervous, moving away from me most of the time. She has just started to wag her tail when I talk to her and has twice shared the sofa, but at a distance. If she moves into a corner, I can give her a brief stroke, otherwise she will only come for a quick sniff of my hand. She is not yet confident enough to take a treat from me. She eats well, preferring to eat alone, but not because of any guarding issues.

Rizzle has chewed toys and played with Petal, my other foster dog, but this is not a regular occurrence. She spends a lot of time alongside Petal. She is getting used to household sounds, dislikes the vacuum cleaner and goes in the garden but is OK with the washing machine, and tolerates the ironing board.

Rizzle will briefly bark if she hears a sound in the garden, eg another dog or voices. At night or if I go out, she sleeps quietly in the lounge with the other dogs. She doesn't enjoy handling at the moment, so I have not made any attempt to put a harness on her. Her toilet training is a work in progress, being clean when the back door is open.

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show us just how inquisitive she can be and is trying her hardest to be brave. Rizzle isn’t quite ready to approach us just yet, but she does follow the lead of her doggy friends and takes lots of comfort from having them around. With plenty of TLC, patience and reassurance, we’re sure it shouldn’t take her too long to come around and start showing her lovely personality.

Rizzle will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training. She will need time to take everything at her own pace and shouldn’t be rushed before she is ready.

Rizzle can live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and will understand that she needs time and space to settle in. She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Max has recently been castrated, and while he was feeling (understandably) sorry for himself for a few days after, he was brilliant going into the vets and during his recovery. Although he has had to wear a buster collar just to stop him licking at the area, he doesn't let that bother him and is such a good boy when you take it off to take him out for a walk and pop it back on when he's back in his kennel and he has been so easy to give his pain relief medication to as well, he really has been a model patient. He is such an easy dog to handle, given his size he is no issue at all.

During his recovery period, Max has only been on short walks so that he doesn't overdo it in the play yards, but slowly this past week he has been spending some time in our agility yard to have a run and you can definitely see that he is back to his full, playful self, running around, chasing a tennis ball and being inquisitive about anything and everything.

Max is a fantastic boy, and any time I spend with him is just so enjoyable and full of love and fun, he is such a special dog, I'm constantly scratching my head wondering why and how he's still here.

Where do I start with the wonderful ball of energy that is Max.

First and foremost, the question I ask myself and almost everyone that meets Max asks too, how on earth is he still waiting?! A young, handsome, intelligent dog who is BARRELS of fun. There’s something about Max that is just so loveable and he truly does capture people’s hearts. Many of the volunteers who walk him are always so happy to see him and enjoy their time together.

Recently we’ve been working on nailing a ‘touch’ command. When Max is focused he is such a rewarding dog to train. Sometimes his desire to please takes over and he waves his paw at me until I have to accept it (and of course reward because he's the goodest boy no matter what). He is also learning to be calmer when greeting people and has even had some gentle fuss from some children too. It remains true that Max cannot be homed with children under the age of 16, but it is so important for Max to have positive interactions with respectful children to prevent any reactivity / fear from developing. It also helps teach him to be calm when meeting new people, especially when they’re smaller than him!

Max brings such a unique type of energy to the rescue, he is such a joyful boy and truly comes alive when he is with his people. I threw Max a 1st birthday party and all of his favourite people came throughout the day to play with him and bring him yummy treats, fuss and cuddles. He had the best day and it was so touching to see how loved he is despite not being in a home.

We are doing our very best to raise Max into a well rounded, well socialised and well adjusted adult dog. However, he is at such a crucial stage in his development and has already spent 5 months in kennels. It’s no place for a young dog to grow up. Nearly half of his life spent in kennels patiently waiting for his second chance to come and take him home.

Despite his size Max really is just a baby and definitely a lap dog too. So if you have a spot on the sofa you can share, Max will happily join you and be the bestest friend anyone could wish for.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Dora
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog in my new home who is my size or larger.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I have spent some time in a home so may know the basics.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Dora is a very worried little girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She spent around 10 months with us before being adopted, but sadly, after only a few months with her adopters, Dora returned to us due to a change in their circumstances.

Unfortunately, Dora has not been dealt the easiest set of cards, but she continues to prove just how brave and strong she is. Despite all the recent changes, she is making new kennel friends, recognising familiar staff members and allowing gentle, slow pets. Dora has made some lovely progress, and it is wonderful to see her continuing to find her feet.

Dora will need a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs. She relies heavily on other dogs for confidence and comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog, preferably her size or larger, to be her friend and help show her the ropes.

Having previously lived in a home, Dora has made some lovely progress, but moving somewhere new will still be a big change. She will need plenty of time, patience and TLC to settle and may need some gentle reminders about her house training.

Dora will now allow gentle strokes, provided you take things slowly and give her the choice to approach. She is still very unsure of handling and does not enjoy being picked up or having her harness put on or taken off. She is very food motivated, however, and will happily come over for some tasty paste! Once wearing her harness, she can walk nicely on a lead.

Dora is looking for a very special home where she can continue to build her confidence and learn to trust the people around her. Perhaps, in time, handling will become less frightening for her, or perhaps she may never fully feel comfortable with it. Either way, she deserves a family who will give her the patience, love and understanding she needs and accept her just as she is.

Unfortunately, Dora has not been dealt the easiest set of cards, but she continues to prove time and time again just how brave and strong she is, putting in the work to find her forever family. I worked with Dora when she was originally here, and the progress she has made is something to be incredibly proud of. Even with all the recent changes, she is making new kennel friends, recognising familiar staff members and allowing gentle, slow pets.

I really hope Dora finds a home filled with love, patience and understanding, where she can continue to build her confidence and learn that handling doesn't have to be such a scary thing. description:

21-11-26 Lori is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder due to having a Grade 4 luxating patella in her left hind leg. She has had X-rays which we are able to send to any potential adopters for them to share with their own vets. Our specialist has advised that she will need specialist surgery to help her mobility, but unfortunately she is too young for this at the moment and it will need to be arranged once her growth plates have fused. Our vet has noted that she has good muscle development and overall walks and runs well with intermittent hopping.

We would love to find adopters who are happy to welcome Lori into their lives as she is now and who would be able to fund her operation when she is old enough. It is estimated that this could cost around £3,000+, depending on which specialist is used, and it would not be covered by insurance as it is a pre-existing condition. We would love for her to settle into a forever home while she is still a puppy, where she can enjoy all the fun of growing up with her own family. If she isn't adopted during this time, we will continue to support her and will arrange her surgery under our care once she is old enough. Lori also has an umbilical hernia that will need to be repaired at the time of her spay, which would need to be after she had recovered from her patella surgery, so her adopters would also need to be aware of this also and agree to have her spayed once she is ready.

Lori is a lovely little girl, but can be quite worried when meeting new people, but once she feels comfortable, her friendly and curious side starts to shine through. Once you spend some time with her, she soon begins to come around and will approach you for some fuss and is happy to be picked up and have her little jumper put on to keep her warm.

Lori would love to find a loving home with adopters who have experience with nervous dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.We would consider homing her with sensible, dog-savvy teenagers.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I’m truly so sad that Dutch is still waiting for his forever home. It’s such a shame that certain breeds can be so easily overlooked.

Dutch is the most sweet, loving, loyal and clever boy. He absolutely loves everyone, has bags of confidence and is always bursting with excitement to say hello to everyone he meets out on a walk.

We've recently started walking Dutch with different friends each day to help him learn to manage some of his reactivity, and honestly, after just one walk, the very next day he was absolutely brilliant!

Dutch isn't reactive because he wants to be difficult, he's simply so excited and eager to say hello that he's still learning how to manage those feelings.

He's such a smart boy and has picked things up so quickly. He just needs someone who will keep that clever brain busy, give him some guidance and help him continue to learn.

Please don't overlook Dutch. There is so much to love about this boy, and we would love nothing more than to see him finally find his forever home.

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home in a semi-rural area.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would love a good sized garden to explore and will need 6ft fences.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was extremely overwhelmed when he first arrived. Although he is still feeling quite overwhelmed to find himself here and can be very worried, especially in new situations, he is making good progress, especially with those people he knows. He was initially very worried when he first met new people, but his circle of friends has grown and he is making more human friends daily. With his favourite people, he is a friendly, affectionate boy.

Cooper will be looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared rescue dogs and though not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. Cooper would be best suited to a home in a rural or semi-rural location and would prefer to go for walks in quiet areas. He will need a secure garden with 6ft fences.

Cooper is especially worried when he finds himself in new or unfamiliar areas, and busy environments with lots of noise, people and hustle and bustle can feel particularly overwhelming for him. He finds visiting the front of the rescue and reception area quite daunting, where there is more activity and unfamiliar sights and sounds. However, when he is given the chance to spend time in a quieter, open yard, he is much more relaxed and happy, showing us that he does best when he has space and a calm environment around him.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet. He has met cats at the rescue fine, and we may consider homing him with a dog-savvy cat.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be. He will require multiple meet and greets with his potential adopters to give him plenty of time to get comfortable with his new family.

He is currently being monitored for left back leg lameness, and has a potential soft tissue injury. He will continue to be monitored by our vets for any further treatment he may need.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

It’s been just over a month since I last did an update on our handsome boy Cooper and since then his confidence has grown even more!

Cooper is now the centre of attention in our big play group, he will engage in play with all the dogs who attend, and even greet any new ones with very good manners! Cooper is also now making lots of human friends with numerous members of staff that he used to be scared of!!

It’s absolutely crazy to see how confident Cooper is being, compared to the day he first arrived! It just goes to show all it take is time, patience and love!

I literally love Cooper with all my heart, watching him turn into the happiest, friendliest boy makes my heart so full!

I really hope his time to be in a home comes soon, he really does have so much love to give when he knows you!

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

name: Luna
description:
I need an adult only home that understands ex-breeders.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

20-11-26 Luna is an extremely nervous lady who has come to us from a breeder. She doesn't quite understand our intentions just yet, so we are having to take things very slowly with her. She would much rather hide away at the back of her kennel and can be quite flighty when worried. Because of this, she will need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to help keep her safe.

Luna relies heavily on her dog friends for reassurance and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing as she learns about home life and begins to build her confidence.

Luna has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about house training and the other basics of home life. Walking on a lead may be too much for her while she is still finding her confidence, so little adventures and sniffs in the garden will be a good place to start.

She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand her needs. A calm and quiet environment, along with plenty of time and patience, will be essential to help her settle at her own pace.

Luna is a very frightened girl who just needs somewhere safe to call home, where she can finally start to feel secure and learn that the world isn't such a scary place.

She has been given the Gift of Life by Julie Coke

name: Mabli
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden with 5ft+ fences.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am underweight and so am being fed little and often to build me up.

14-11-26 Mabli is a worried girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was quite shut down, but she has started to settle in and although still very shy, she will now approach us although quickly loses her confidence again. You can tell that she's super smart and is watching and learning with every interection.

Mabli clearly hasn't experienced much before and is very worried and unsure about handling at the moment so she will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with nervous dogs as well as experience with the breed and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy, gentle teenagers aged 13+.

Mabli relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance, so will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and show her how wonderful life can be.

Despite her worries Mabli is an incredibly gentle soul andis happy to sit quietly beside us, and she particularly enjoyed spending time with staff near the pond, simply sitting together and taking in all the surroundings. She has also shown some interest in chasing and playing with a ball with us too. We hope that, with time and patience, she will begin to feel safer and discover that human company can be a lovely thing.

As Mabli has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about home life and new skills like house training. She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness, but will need more practice to gain confidence with this. Once she has settled in, we think she would love to go on lots of walks and adventures and would benefit from an active home with adopters who will keep her both mentally and physically stimulated.

Mabli has arrived underweight and will need a nutritious diet to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. She is currently having four meals a day with us, and we hope to see an improvement soon. This monitoring will need to continue in her new home. She has also arrived with a cut on her nose, which we will monitor to make sure it stays clean and heals nicely.

Mabli is a gentle, sensitive girl who has clearly had a lot to take in. We know she will need time to find her confidence, but we hope that with a quiet home, a reassuring canine friend and lots of kindness, she will eventually discover the comfort and happiness of being truly loved.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Loyal
description:
I need a calm and quiet adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

05-11-26 Loyal has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a very nervous girl who is feeling quite overwhelmed at the moment. She isn't used to being handled and finds this quite worrying at the moment and if pushed out of her comfort zone may panic. At the moment, she prefers to watch you curiously from a safe distance rather than approach and she is very weary of strangers.

Loyal will be looking for a calm and quietadult-onlyhome with kind and understanding adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs. She will need a family who can give her the time and space she needs to settle in at her own pace, without putting any pressure on her. Loyal will need careful handling and not be pushed into situations she is not ready for. She will flash her teeth when she is feeling uncomfortable so will require experienced and patient adopters.

Loyal relies on other dogs for comfort and so will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and take her under their wing.

Loyal has never lived in a home before, so she will need help learning all about home life and new skills like house training. She will need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness, first practicing around the home and garden. Her adopters will need to be prepared to take things slowly and give her plenty of reassurance as she adjusts to her new world.

With kindness, patience and a safe place to call her own, we hope Loyal will gradually learn that she has nothing to worry about and that life can be full of lovely things

Loyal has been given the Gift of Life by Lauren Hyslop
