name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I have been spayed and am ready to find my forever home!

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to “Pop”, so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise and mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is a quick learner who has mastered “sit” and is currently learning “touch”. She picks things up quickly, which is helping with her ongoing muzzle training.

Pop walks beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles, so she will need an active home that enjoys getting out and about and helping her learn new things. She is doing well with her training and is now walking alongside calm dogs, which is lovely progress. However, she is not yet comfortable wearing a muzzle for long periods, and we are continuing to build her confidence with this gradually. The aim is to help her become comfortable wearing one when needed, so she can be kept safe around other dogs in busier areas in the future. At the rescue, under supervision with her surroundings managed, she is enjoying muzzle free play time with Lassie so it is possible she will not always need a muzzle for mixing with her canine friends.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Although she is making progress with carefully managed walks alongside calm dogs, she can still become reactive when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and committed to continuing her positive, reward-based training to help her feel more comfortable around dogs when out and about.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine. She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle, ongoing training and consistency she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

Pop has been making really good progress and has even made a friend here that she mixes with unmuzzled, she seems to enjoy a little bit of a play but then needs to have a little pause during some play dates when her friend gets a little bit too playful and overwhelms her. After a couple of minute of calm she will happily play again but it's important that her new people don't rush her with her socialisation, and instead, just take it at a pace that Pop is happy and comfortable with. She is very good at communicating when she's feeling a bit overwhelmed so you just have to listen to her and take her out of the stressful situation.

We are still muzzle training her to help her with her doggy social skills, this is very much a work-in-progress as we want her to be 100% happy with one step before moving on to the next, but I am very proud of her for reaching the stage of putting her nose in on queue and holding it there for a few seconds before getting more tasty paste.

In general she is such a happy ball of energy who just wants someone who will take her on adventures and truly be her best friend.

Pop can be homed with dog-savvy teens but they must be understanding of her getting a little mouthy when over-excited and although this is something that she is improving on, we don't want her new adopters to be worried by this behaviour if it were to happen in the home. We ignore it and reward her for being calm, which is all it usually takes for her to stop and then we continue with something fun, she also will usually grab a toy when excited in her kennel, so we are in the process of teaching her to do this on command to help her know where to place all that excited energy safely.

I can see her making a family incredibly happy, she really does have so much to offer the right home.

Pops is such a beautiful, smart girl who is super friendly with people. She has just mastered "sit" and is currently learning "touch". She picks things up pretty quickly, which is also helping her with her muzzle training.

Pops isn't sociable with other dogs currently, but this is something we're working on by taking her on walks with calm dogs at a distance. Once she is happily muzzle trained, we will work up to safe mixes with dogs who are a good match.

She does need to be an only dog in the home, and her people will need to keep up the training we've put in place to help her feel more comfortable around other dogs when out and about in public.

She walks absolutely beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles and miles, so she will need an active home who enjoys helping their dog feel happier and learn new things.

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

name: Hatty
description:
I need an experienced adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I've never met cats so I'm unsure!

I'm a bit of a Houdini and will need a secure garden to keep me safe.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need careful introduction.

I'm still learning house training, lead walking, and other basics of home life.

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

30-09-26 Hatty originally came to us from a breeder, and was adopted for a period of time, and was sadly returned to our care due to her adopter becoming unwell. She managed a recent vet visit incredibly well considering how worried she can be, allowing the vet to examine her and administer her vaccinations while she was safely cuddled in her blanket. We know that the right home for Hatty is out there, and that with someone who truly understands her, she can form an incredibly special bond.Hatty is a very worried little lady who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She finds human interaction incredibly stressful and can still be very timid and defensive when she feels she is going to be handled. However, she has made some lovely progress in her foster home and is showing us that, with the right person and plenty of patience, she can learn to feel safe.

Hatty will still need a blanket to help her feel comfortable when she needs to be picked up, and she can become frightened enough to toilet herself when she is worried about being handled. Once she is safely settled, she will allow gentle strokes around her face, head and back, although she is not comfortable with her feet being touched. Her foster home has found that she is happiest when she is given plenty of space and allowed to approach things at her own pace.

Hatty absolutely loves other dogs and is particularly happy around other Dachshunds. She gets very excited to see her dog friends and enjoys being around them, so she will need a confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel safe and show her the ropes. She enjoys having a cosy space of her own to retreat to, but also loves being able to relax on the sofa alongside the other dogs.

Hatty is very treat motivated and will happily come over for treats, which is a lovely way for her adopters to build a positive relationship with her. She is content plodding around, observing what is going on and enjoying the company of her canine friends. She can be destructive if left alone, so her adopters will need to be prepared for this and ensure she has plenty of safe things to occupy her.

Hatty will need a very special home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand just how frightening the world can feel for her. She will need a quiet, adult-only home with someone who is around most of the time and who can give her the time and space she needs without placing expectations on her. She will need gentle handling and continued support with things such as toilet training and lead training, although walks may not be something she becomes comfortable with.

Hatty is not going to be an easy dog to rehome, but she is a very special and frightened girl who deserves someone willing to see past her worries. With a confident canine companion, a quiet home and an adopter who can give her the time and patience she needs, we believe Hatty can continue to flourish and discover just how lovely life can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Juice
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have learned how to walk on a lead and am enjoying going for walks.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

Juice came to us from a breeder and when she first arrived, she was understandably very shy and overwhelmed by everything around her. She wanted to trust people but was nervous about approaching, often hovering nearby and watching with interest before her worries got the better of her. She has since moved into foster and has made some lovely progress and is settling in well. Juice is still cautious, but she now follows her fosterers around the house and will approach for fuss when they offer their hand to her. She particularly loves belly rubs and will completely relax and close her eyes!

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. Although she does rely on other dogs for comfort, she can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so she will need a calm, relaxed resident dog who will not disturb her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and on one occasion she did nip her fosterer when they stroked her in her bed. Her new family will therefore need to be confident managing this behaviour, recognising her body language and ensuring she is always left undisturbed when she is resting.

Juice had never lived in a home before moving to foster, but she is already settling in wonderfully. Her toilet training is going really well and she has only had 2 accidents in the home so far. She has also learned all about walking on a lead and harness and is now becoming more confident wearing her harness and she is starting to enjoy her walks. She is also beginning to understand that the home is a safe place, happily relaxing and sleeping near her fosterers and enjoying the company of their resident dog.

Juice will be looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand that she is still learning to trust and who will allow her to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She has already come such a long way in a short time, and we hope that with the right family, she will continue to blossom into a happy and loving companion.

She has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Juice has been given the Gift of Life by Holly Kantolinna

Juice has settled in really well. She is still cautious but follows us around the house although backs off if we approach her as she prefers it if you put your hand out to her. She will then approach us, sniff our hand and accept fuss and scratches. She loves having scratches but her favourite are belly rubs and she will close her eyes and completely relax!

She sleeps well over night in her bed on the floor in our bedroom and will wake us up by walking around the room when she needs to go to toilet. Her toilet training is going really well and apart from 2 accidents early on she goes in the garden either asking to go out or when the back door is open taking herself out to go.

She is getting more confident having her harness on for walk and as long as you put it on slowly, she is happy to have it on. She is starting to walk really well on her lead and enjoys her walks and plenty of sniffs! She has met a few dogs on her walks and as long as they are not too energetic and boisterous she seems happy to meet them and have a sniff! She is ok walking along roads but does startle if there are any loud or sudden noises.

She loves being with us in the house and although she doesn't sit right next to us she enjoys being close by and really relaxes and sleeps. She enjoys being with our resident dog but is also happy to follow us outside or sit with us when our dog isn't there. She's also happy travelling in the car with our dog.

She hasn't mastered going up and down stairs yet so at present we are carrying her up and down. She is starting to go up a few small steps on her walks.

She enjoys her food and will sometimes take treats or food from our hands.  She is a lovely girl who has really progressed in the short time that we have had her and is continuing to develop her confidence.

Juice will need an experienced, adult only home with adopters who can understand and manage her nervousness and recognise when she needs space. She can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so any resident dog will need to be calm and relaxed and not likely to bother her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and, on one occasion, she did nip when she was stroked resting. Her adopters will therefore need to be confident in managing this behaviour, ensuring she is left undisturbed in her bed and giving her the space she needs to feel safe and comfortable.

Juice has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin the next chapter of her life.

She is a wonderful little lady who is feeling a little shy and overwhelmed at the moment, but she is trying so hard to be brave. Juice is already showing lovely signs that she wants to trust people. She will quietly hover nearby, watching you with interest and looking as though she would really like to come over for a gentle fuss, but at the last moment her worries get the better of her. We think that with time, patience, love and plenty of reassurance, her confidence will continue to grow and her true personality will begin to shine through.

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time and who will let her make progress without putting any pressure on her. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her that life is full of good things.

As Juice has never lived in a home before, everything will be a brand new experience for her. She will need help with housetraining, learning about household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to all the sights and sounds of family life. She is also yet to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, so her adopters will need to introduce this gently and positively as her confidence grows.

Juice is a lovely girl with so much potential. With a patient family by her side and a canine friend to guide her, we are sure she will blossom into a happy and much-loved companion.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I would need to be the only animal in the home.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, and new environments and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed. Even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him. He was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet, adult-only home without resident or visiting children. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house, so he will need a home without too many visitors and where he can be placed in a separate room when people do come over. His adopters will also need to be willing to meet him multiple times before adoption so that he has the opportunity to develop a bond and build trust with them.

Gabriel is a very sensitive boy who feels anxious about a lot of things. During his time here we are trying to help him feel more comfortable by giving him the tools to know how to be more relaxed in these scary situations. To Gabriel, new people are very scary and he feels that he needs to tell them to go away by barking and lunging, when put in poor situations this has led to him having a bite history. He is a very sweet dog but he has very little he trusts in this world and unfortunately humans are top of that list at the moment. With people who have earned his trust he is exceptionally sweet and loving, he loves to give you cuddles and he really thinks he should be a lap dog. When introductions are done slowly and in a manner that he can cope with he will allow that person into his circle reasonably quickly and then he gets very excited to see them.

As he has had very little in this world he does become exceptionally attached to his trusted humans and doesn't like to share them with other dogs or other people, so he is looking for a home with a maximum of two people and will need to be the only dog in the home. Adopters with experience of guarding behaviours are essential to help him succeed in his next home and make sure it really will be his forever home.

Gabriel walks nicely on his harness and gets very excited to see dogs when out and about but is wary of strangers walking past, for this reason he is muzzled when out as it keeps him safe in the event of someone getting too close or trying to touch him.

He has shown signs of resource guarding his food here and any high value long lasting treats. He has Kongs as he is happy for the empty Kong to be removed from his kennel once he feels he's finished with it, but these are things that will have to be managed in his new home. It would be a good idea to limit his access to the kitchen in the home to avoid the possibility of him getting things that he may be inclined to guard, especially until he settles and the bond has been built with him to ensure that he trusts that you won't take things away from him without him getting something higher value in its place.

Gabriel socialises well with other dogs here and does enjoy chasing dogs around our big play yard here, so having the opportunity to continue making friends with playful dogs in his new home is necessary to keep him happy and help him to continue to grow in confidence. Someone will be incredibly lucky to have Gabriel as their companion, they will just have to understand that he does require the time and effort to make sure he progresses and starts to see the world is less scary than he thinks it is.

Gabriel will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Gabriel is still waiting for his forever home, I don't know what it's going to take for people to notice this handsome man.

Gabriel recently had a play date with Margate who some of you may have heard of, they went to spend a few hours at a nearby lake with two of our members of staff, and he had a blast. He was on a long line and was free to explore wherever he wanted.

He was so well behaved during the walk, with Margate, the two staff members and when they stopped for ice cream after. He just loves being out adventuring, he wants to sniff everything and explore the world around him, needless to say he was knackered when he returned, had his dinner and went to bed, the sign of a good day.

Gabriel loved his time and the lake, so much so that I'm planning on taking him for another adventure soon that he will hopefully love just as much.

Today I got to spend more time with Gabriel than I usually would so I took advantage of that and we went for a much longer walk.... As usual he was brilliant, he listens, if we need to move out of the way for a car he'll listen to me and move off the road to the side, if he's walking slightly ahead and I call him he stops and turns back.

We also sat around the other side of the rescue where it's usually busier as I want to get him used to being in busier areas and being around people he doesn't know, as he can be a bit reactive.... He did so well, it was fairly busy so he was a little unsure at first but the longer we stayed the better he was, he was good with others around him too, he has come such a long way, but this is something I'm going to keep on working on with him for the foreseeable as we don't know what life he'll have outside of here and he may need to used to busier areas.

We also played with a puzzle feeder today, which he decided would be fun to pick up with his mouth and drop it on the floor to get the treats out faster, he really is a funny boy, but he's super smart too and is quick to pick up tricks especially when there's treats involved.

He really is every Bocker lovers dream and he always gets so overlooked.

He is muzzle trained, and would need to wear his muzzle when meeting new people, dogs or at the vets, but he's also just a big softy who gives the loveliest cwtches and kisses, to be a part of his gang is such an amazing feeling and he shows his affection for you so clearly when he loves you.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs and will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Crumble
description:
I need an adult-only, experienced home where I can feel safe and loved.

I want to be the only dog in the house. No cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I love my walks so one or two a day would be great!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Crumble is a lovely lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings. She seems to be gaining confidence each day, which is wonderful to see.

While she can still be sensitive and appreciates having her space respected, it’s clear that Crumble simply needed time to feel safe. With gentle reassurance and plenty of TLC, her true personality is beginning to shine through. She is a gentle soul who responds best to calm, kind interactions and slow introductions.

She would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where she can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with her new family.

As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training and learning everyday routines. She will need a home without cats as she is overly interested.

We are looking for an experienced, adult-only home where Crumble can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. A quiet household with understanding adopters who are happy to let her take things slowly will allow her to truly flourish. With the right people, time, and lots of love, Crumble will make a wonderfully rewarding companion.

On arrival, our vets noted that Crumble had a Grade 2 luxating patella. During her time with us she has shown very intermittent lameness, mostly only seen when she’s getting up from laying down for a long time. She was sent for x-rays which showed potential damage to her left cruciate ligament, as well as hip dysplasia in her right hip. She is currently managing very well with rest and pain relief, and we will work on building correct muscle tone to support her as well as slow introductions to controlled exercise and physio.

My ‘little croissant’! She is as sweet and squishy as a croissant. But don’t be fooled, Crumble is sweet and sassy and rags Criss Cross around as if he wasn’t bigger than her. She nibbles on her kennel mums when she sees her harness or gets overexcited, she body slams when she’s having zoomies and, when given the opportunity to cuddle, she never wants me to leave her kennel because she just wants her friends to stay for a little while longer.

Crumble loves her toys and has not been known to destroy them. She loves her walks and is looking for a home that can provide her with a whole lot of love, fuss and an abundance of soft beds, knowing that Crumble will ultimately choose to lay on the cold floor the majority of the time!

I was very eager to say hello to my little croissant, haven’t worked with Crumble for a little over a month, but she was a bit reluctant to approach me. Once I allowed her a little time to recognise me and give me a standard sniff, the very friendly, bouncy little lady almost tackled me with love. Bum scratches galore!

I showed her the harness, and she was beaming, giving little excited nibbles of my hands to show just how excited she was to spend time with me, an old friend, out of the kennels.

She is currently on kennel rest and has been instructed to have one small walk a day to keep her legs strong, and it is quite a challenge to keep this girly still.

I hope Crumble finds a home before Christmas because seeing such a happy girly who can live alone still living in kennels, as much as we do our best to ensure Crumble is well taken care of, is sad. She deserves the love of a home, a comfy bed and unlimited scratches and walks!

Crumble is one of those ladies that you may need to work harder to earn their trust initially but once she loves you she truly is besotted and becomes very excited to see you every time you appear. She is very playful with her best friend Criss Cross but is very dog selective otherwise, she has recently been approved to start going for short walks daily after being on kennel rest and she is very happy to be able to go for a walk with Criss Cross and have all the sniffs again.

Crumble can be unsure about noises and her instinct is to go to her safe space in the back of her kennel and wait for the scary thing to go away but she does take comfort when her trusted people go in and sit with her to let her know that she is okay.She may be looking for a particular set up with very special people who understand her and love all of her quirks, but when she finds it she will make them smile and laugh every single day, this girl has so much love and personality to share with you once you've made her feel safe around you.

Crumble is the most incredible girl who loves her humans once she has bonded with you. She has such a huge personality and makes all of her kennel mums and dads laugh every single day.

She absolutely loves playing with her best friend Criss Cross and she loves splashing in water when it's warm weather.

She's one of those exceptional girls who will make someone incredibly lucky and give them so much love and fun once they've put in the time to earn her trust and build that bond with her.

There’s not a bad word you could say about this girly pop. She is goofy, affectionate, playful, friendly and gaining confidence by the day! She has been trying her best to be kennel clean, no encouragement needed.

She is a staff favourite and that girls little teefys are part of her personality! Nibbling at you to show you just how much she loves to play with you, entertains her pal Criss cross and her kennel mums in the yard.

She belongs in a home where her people can show her the best doggy life imaginable while also understanding that Crumble has also not known much of the world and requires a bit of patience and care when handling her.

Taking every opportunity to play and zoom around with her best friend, Criss Cross.Her confidence is growing and enjoying her walks and greeting new people at her own free will as long as she is guaranteed some fuss or treats.

She enjoys sprawling out on the floor with her chew toy just enjoying the vibes.When she finds her home she will be very eager in sharing her affectionate nature with her family

Crumble is becoming a very happy chow now and has recently discovered that there's no limit on zoomies. She does get along with her chow friend, Criss Cross, but isn't keen on other dogs, so is looking for a home as an only. She is wary of people initially, but once you've gained her trust she becomes your absolute best mate. She loves her walks and gets very excited when she sees you bringing her harness towards her. She's a big foodie too and loves treats.

Crumble is coming on so beautifully and it truly makes my heart melt. Today we had some cuddle and play time in her kennel, and it was such a special moment. For a girl who once wasn’t very happy with touch, she’s now rolling over for belly rubs, snuggling in her bed, and even playing “paw paw” with me.

She’s also learning about wearing a harness and is improving every day. If you have a Crumble shaped hole in your life, she really is something special.

Crumble is a worried lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings.

Crumble will need a confident and friendly resident dog who can help guide her and show her the ropes. As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training, lead walking, and learning everyday routines. But will need to take things slow to start with some garden sniffs adventures on the lead may be too scary to start.

Crumble has a previous bite wound inside her ear, which is currently being treated.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Criss Cross
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I'd prefer to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can now walk on a lead and harness and enjoy my walks.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Criss Cross, a big-hearted, sensitive lad who has come to us from a breeder and is slowly learning to find his confidence in the world. When Criss Cross arrived as a worried soul, needing extra patience, understanding, and gentle care. He had very little formal handling in his past, and early on could be grumbly or anxious when unsure. He required slow, careful introductions to people, places, and experiences while he started to understand his new surroundings.

While Criss Cross can still be a little shy when meeting new people, once he feels comfortable his affectionate side really shines through. He actively seeks out fuss and cuddles and has become quite the cuddle bug, often trying to return kisses to the people he trusts. He is learning his manners well and responds nicely to calm, consistent guidance.

Criss Cross is growing in confidence with his harness training and now enjoys daily walks beyond the rescue. He has even started greeting some people on his walks for a hello and perhaps a treat or a fuss. He can still feel a little unsure if people are behind him, but gentle encouragement and reassurance help him relax and continue exploring the world around him.

He has also started learning about kennel cleanliness, with staff helping him practice good toilet habits to make the transition into a home life easier for him in the future. When enjoying some quiet time on his own, Criss Cross loves exploring his toy collection, especially anything involving treats or food puzzles.

Criss Cross would prefer to be the only dog in the home so he can fully relax and enjoy all the attention for himself.

He will need a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who can continue helping him build confidence at his own pace. He also appreciates having a quiet space at mealtimes where he feels safe and secure. Criss Cross will need a home without cats as he is overly interested in them.

Criss Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet-natured gentle giant with so much love to give. With patience, understanding, endless bum scratches and plenty of tasty treats, he has every chance to flourish into the loyal and devoted companion he is meant to be.

Criss Crosswill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

I adore this sweet boy. Criss Cross has completely stolen my heart and shown just how much love, trust and affection he has to give once he feels safe with someone. He really is a real-life Winnie the Pooh.

Criss Cross is easily scared by the big wide world because that’s all he’s ever known, but in the time he’s been here at the rescue, he has been able to learn, trust and have hope. It has not been a smooth journey, but Criss Cross shows just how much trust and loyalty he has in the staff who look after him daily. I hope his future family take their time to gain his trust because once they do, they’ll see such a difference in our sweet boy!

To give you an insight, when Criss Cross knows you, he has zoomies, thinks he’s light as a feather and loves a fuss. He loves to lick our faces, although we try not to encourage it as he has been known to have smelly breath! He likes to play with his toys, even destroying a few soft ones, and although he hides under his bed when the show round is there, he will brave it if his favourite people are in his kennel with him. He loves his kennel, and if you have his harness, you best believe he is running rings around you to get it on! He loves exploring, especially with his friend Crumble, has slowly been socialising with other dogs and meeting other staff members, and does his very best to be kennel clean.

I'd love for Criss Cross to find a home where he can experience all the great firsts in life, whether that's discovering if he prefers a cosy couch to a dog bed or getting to explore a garden of his very own. He has so much love to give, and I hope someone will give him the chance to show them just how special he is.

Criss Cross is the most sensitive soul who is easily affected by life and it breaks my heart, he's looking for a very special human who would take him under their wing and give him all that he needs to thrive and cope with how scary the world can be. Whilst his best friend Crumble has been on kennel rest Criss Cross has really been struggling to be brave enough to go for road walks, he's only felt comfortable walking around the quiet field that's behind his section as he can cope with it there and he feels safe. Since Crumble has been given the go ahead to start going for little walks daily again he has been enjoying his road walks in her company. This just highlights how sensitive he is and how much he struggles in certain situations. He did go for a couple of walks with a collie but he didn't get much comfort from her company so didn't really enjoy them.I know he needs a very specific person who will love him exactly for who he is and who has the right set up to help him have a truly wonderful life as he deserves. I just hope they're out there somewhere looking for a big bundle of love who just needs some understanding to be able to help his cheeky and funny personality shine through.

Criss Cross has been doing very well socialising with other dogs, he walks politely next to calm dogs and even had a muzzled play date the other day. His best friend Crumble is currently on kennel rest, so he only gets to see her very briefly whilst on lead, but he always runs to the front of her kennel to say hello before going back to his own kennel.

He is such a sweet boy who adores his people once he trusts you. He just needs positive introductions to feel comfortable with new people. Very proud of the progress he's been making and we'll continue to work on his doggy social skills.

Criss Cross is such a sweetheart! He is loyal to his friend Crumble, his kennel mums and dads. He’s still greeting everyone on walks with a bit of caution but once he’s recognised you, you’re considered family.

He’s going on occasional independent walks to gain his confidence but he is always looking for Crumble to keep him company. He’s very cautious of new things however day by day his confidence is growing and with his trust in his kennel mums he always runs back to check they’re okay, showing you just how brave he is and continues to be, so when the right home finds him….they will have to earn his trust and give him the patience and love he truly deserves.

This distinguished gent is progressing so well, every day!

He has started to get in the practice of being kennel clean, one of his kennel mums likes to come in a little early to help him practice this so when he finds his forever home it might be a little less stressful learning toilet training skills properly.

Criss Cross is even getting more adventurous greeting people on his daily walks now just to  say hello and maybe scoring a treat or fuss, and even recognising some of the staff when they visit him.

He is protective of Crumble and always looks to see her catching up on their daily walks, and enjoys playing with her or being near watching over her. But when he has his solo kennel time, he has been exploring his personal toy collection, anything with a treat in it and he’s happy. This cuddle bug deserves a home with endless bum scratches and scrumptious treats

This handsome guy is progressing every day! And showing his kennel mums just how much of a sweetheart he is. He is an affectionate goofball once he’s comfortable with you. He enjoys playing with his chow friend Crumble and he loves getting love from her and his kennel mums. He loves to jump up to have his harness put on, refusing to stand still because he gets so excited to go out and explore with Crumble.

Criss Cross will now even allow some of his part time kennel mums and dads to give him attention too. He is still very cautious of new people but is slowly meeting new people and remembering them!

With some time his new family will find out just how special Criss Cross is!

Criss Cross has made incredible progress over the last few days. He used to hide and grumble when people approached his kennel, but this has changed massively!

Now, Criss Cross comes up to the kennel door and wags his tail, getting very excited to see people. Spending time with this handsome boy brings me so much joy; I often find myself straying from my section just to sneak in five minutes of cuddles.

Criss Cross is still looking for a quiet, gentle home and someone who will take things slow while he gets to know them.

Criss-Cross has grown into an incredibly sociable and interactive boy, although he can still be a little shy when first meeting new people. Once he feels comfortable, he actively seeks out attention and loves a cuddle, often trying to give kisses in return. Criss-Cross is a big lad and is still learning his manners; when he’s excited he can occasionally use his size to try and barge past, but he responds well to clear, firm verbal guidance.

He will need a quiet area to enjoy his meals, as this helps him feel more secure. Criss-Cross is doing very well with his harness training and has already ventured out of the rescue for walks, managing a good distance down the road. He can still feel a little unsure if people are walking behind him, and one of his endearing little quirks is that he finds reassurance if you turn and face him while walking backwards. Criss-Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet and gentle giant who will thrive in an active, patient and understanding home.

Criss Cross is a very worried soul who has come to us from a breeder, and is needing extra patience, understanding, and tender care. He appears to have had very little formal handling in his past and can be grumbly or anxious when he feels uncomfortable. He requires slow, careful introductions and time to begin to understand the world around him.

Criss Cross would thrive in an adult-only home with experienced owners who can provide the reassurance and consistency he needs to start building trust. He is still learning the basics of house training and walking on a lead, so his adopters will need to be patient and gentle as he gradually discovers confidence. He will need an understanding and kind resident dog in the home he can look to as he continues to learn and trust.

This sweet, sensitive boy is not yet ready for the full bustle of the world, but with time, quiet encouragement, and safe garden sniffing adventures, he will slowly open up and reveal the loyal companion he can be. Criss Cross will need a calm, loving home where his cautious nature is respected and nurtured and where he can finally feel safe and truly belong.

Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Bella
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption. Read below for more!

Bella is a frightened little girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She has now been with us for over a month and, although she is still very shut down, we have started to see some lovely little breakthroughs. She will not yet approach us for fuss and still does her best to keep her distance, but she is slowly beginning to show us what she is capable of.

We are incredibly proud of the progress Bella has made with her harness training. To our surprise, she is doing much better than we initially expected! She now walks well to and from the yard and has even started venturing down to our big play yard, which involves walking along the road. She can still become spooked at times, so her adopters will need to be patient and understand that she is not yet ready for busy places or lots of new experiences. She will need to continue building her confidence at her own pace.

Once in the big yard, Bella is starting to run around more freely and enjoy spending time with the other dogs. When it is time to leave, she will follow us towards the gate before finding her safe corner and allowing us to put her lead on. These may seem like small things, but they are wonderful steps forward for such a frightened girl.

At the moment, Bella is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends, and we feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with another kind and confident dog for support and companionship. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us, but for now, we feel having a canine friend to help her feel safe will be important.

As Bella has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Although her harness training is progressing well, her new family will need to continue this gently and patiently. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that building trust with her will take time. She is not yet ready to seek affection, so her family must be happy to let her settle at her own pace without expecting too much of her too soon.

Due to her nervous nature, Bella will need a very secure garden with 6ft fencing to keep her safe.

Bella is a worried little soul, and she still has a long way to go, but we are so proud of the progress she has made already. Seeing her begin to explore the big yard, enjoy time with other dogs and take those first steps on her harness gives us hope for her future. We desperately hope someone will take a chance on this special girl and offer her the quiet, patient home she needs to feel safe and discover the life she deserves.

Bella has had a possible seizure while in our care, and is being monitored by the vets.

Bella has been given the Gift of Life by Olivia Coles

Oh little Bella is a heart breaker, she’s been with us over a month now and is still very shut down. She won’t approach us for a fuss and still tries her best to keep away from us.

We have had some break through though in which we are super proud of her, she’s now walking on a harness and to our surprise is actually doing so much better than we thought, she walks well to and from the yard and has even started to venture down to our big yard which involves walking along the road. She can still have her times of being spooked and is going to need patient adopters who won’t expect to take her out to busy places just yet.

Down the big yard she’s starting to run around more freely and enjoy the time with the other dogs, when it’s time to go we just have to walk to the gate and she will follow us and then find her corner and allow us to be the lead.

We are truly so proud of the process she’s made and we hope someone takes a chance on her soon.

Bella is a frightened girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.

She is showing little glimpses of curiosity, but is very flighty at the moment. She will not yet approach us and will try to run away if she feels she can. Once cornered, Bella shuts down and accepts handling, although she is clearly very unsure of what is happening around her.

At the moment, Bella is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for Bella to be rehomed with another dog for support and companionship. That said, we will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see whether she could eventually adapt to being an only dog.

As Bella has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience and understanding she will need.

Due to her nervous nature Bella will need a very secure garden with 6ft fencing to keep her safe.

Bella has a worried little soul, but those glimpses of curiosity give us hope that there is a more confident girl waiting to emerge. With time, patience and the reassurance of a kind canine companion, we hope she can begin to feel safe, find her paws and enjoy the fresh start she deserves.

name: Iggy
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

Iggy is a scared little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now been with us for almost two months and, although she has made some lovely progress, she has had very little interest so far.

Iggy's biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she can crouch down and tremble with fear, but she is slowly learning that people can be kind and that she is safe. She is beginning to show more interest in people and, by watching the other dogs around her, has started running towards her carers' hands and giving them a little boop! She has also started taking treats, which is a huge step forward for this very special girl.

Iggy takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her build confidence, learn to trust and discover the joys of home life. She absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends and enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine.

As Iggy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns about house training and settles into a new routine. She is still new to lead walking and will need continued, gentle encouragement as she learns. She will need adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs who understand how frightened she can be and are prepared to give her plenty of time and patience.

Iggy can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and able to allow her to settle at her own pace.

Iggy has been assessed by our vets and has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These are not causing her any issues at present and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet, and they should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Iggy is a wonderful girl who has already shown us that, with the right canine companion and plenty of patience, she can take those important little steps forward. We hope the right family will give her the chance to continue blossoming and discover how lovely life can be.

Iggy has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

This wonderful girl is Iggy! It’s been almost two months since she arrived, and although she is doing incredibly well, sadly she has had very little to no interest so far.

As a Frenchie / Bulldog lover myself, I took to this girl instantly, and she has now moved into my section. She has settled in so well and walks beautifully on her harness.

Iggy’s biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she crouches down as though she wishes the ground would swallow her up, and she trembles with fear. Every day, I sit beside her in her kennel and gently stroke the side of her face, reassuring her that she doesn’t need to be afraid anymore. She is slowly learning that not everyone is there to hurt her, but I can only imagine what this poor girl may have experienced in her life.

What makes her progress even more special is seeing her learn from the other dogs around her. When they come over for fuss, Iggy has started running towards my hands and giving them a little boop! She has even started taking treats, which is a huge step for this very special girl.

Iggy absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends. She enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine, and I could happily sit and watch her all day when she’s feeling relaxed and happy.

But as wonderful as her time here has been, I know that what Iggy truly needs now is a home of her own. A quiet, patient and understanding home where she can continue to learn that the world isn’t such a scary place, at her own pace, surrounded by people who will never give up on her.

Iggy is a scared little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show an interest in people and will cautiously approach if you crouch down to her level, but she quickly loses confidence if movements are too fast or overwhelming. She simply needs time to learn that people can be kind. Iggy takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she builds her confidence, learns to trust, and discovers the joys of home life. As Iggy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns all about house training and settles into a new routine. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who are sensible and allow her time to settle in. She will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeders as she can be nervous and will need a home that understands her needs.

She is new to lead walking and will need continued, gentle encouragements in her new home as she continues to learn. Iggy is a wonderful girl who just needs time, patience and lots of TLC. With an understanding family and a confident canine companion by her side, we're sure she will continue to blossom and find her paws.

Iggy has been assessed by our vets who have noted that she has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These aren't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet and her adopters should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

name: Rhea
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have bilateral cataracts & I will be spayed before adoption!

08-11-26 Rhea has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a worried little girl who is a little overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment. She can be quite timid when she first meets you, but after a while she does start to come out of her shell and will accept a fuss with a little waggy tail. She is also starting to become quite nosey and inquisitive, which is lovely to see.

Rhea will be looking for a loving home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She currently relies on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to as she begins to find her feet. Rhea does show some signs of resource guarding around food and can grumble at other dogs, so she will need to be fed separately from any other dogs in her new home. This is specifically around sharing food with other dogs, rather than with people. Her adopters will need to be confident in managing this and helping her feel comfortable at mealtimes.

Rhea has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about the routines of home life, including house training and walking on a lead. Having a confident canine companion to show her the ropes will be a big help as she builds her confidence and starts to discover the world outside the rescue.

Rhea could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Rhea is a sweet, timid girl who will need a little extra time, kindness and reassurance to help her find her paws. With the right home and a lovely doggy friend by her side, we hope she will gradually grow in confidence and learn to enjoy all the comforts of home life.

Rhea has arrived with bilateral cataracts, which does not seem to be bothering her at this time but will need to be monitored in her future home.

Rhea has been given the Gift of Life by Rosalind Steven

name: Jinx
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a sore eye that is being monitored.

Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder. He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. However, after just over a month in our care, his personality is slowly beginning to shine through. Although he remains very wary and unsure, he is starting to make lovely little steps forward. He now gets excited when he sees a familiar face, happily wagging his tail and sniffing a hand, even if he isn't quite ready for anyone to come too close. These may seem like small steps, but for Jinx they are huge achievements, and it is wonderful to see his confidence growing.

Jinx has also begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He is now venturing down to our big play yard, where his playful puppy side is starting to emerge. It is lovely to see him becoming a little more curious about the world around him as he gradually learns that he is safe.

Jinx will need a kind and confident resident dog in his new home, as this will be a much-needed support system to help him settle and gain confidence. We have not yet cat tested him, but given what we have seen so far, we feel it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.

As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. His harness training is progressing well, but his adopters will need to continue this gently and at his own pace. He will need a quiet, experienced home with people who understand ex-breeding dogs and appreciate that building trust with him will take considerable time, patience and kindness.

Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He may also need to be muzzled for formal handling, such as veterinary visits, to help keep everyone safe and make these experiences as comfortable as possible for him.

Jinx arrived with a sore eye, so we are continuing to clean it and make sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.

Jinx still has a long way to go, but he is making progress every day, and it is lovely to see his gentle, playful personality beginning to emerge. He needs a very special home filled with patience and love, where his adopters understand that trust will take time and are happy to celebrate every little achievement along the way. With the support of a kind canine companion and people who will let him move at his own pace, we hope Jinx will continue to blossom and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.

Jinx has been given the Gift of Life by Lesley Beattie

Jinx has now been with us just over a month, and although Jinx is still a very scared boy, his personality is slowly starting to shine through. Jinx has now begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He even now adventures down to our big play yard where his puppy side is really starting to show!  Jinx also now gets really excited to see me, he doesn’t allow me very close but he will happily wag his tail, and sniff my hand!

This might sound like the smallest thing, but for myself and Jinx this is a massive win! Every day is confidence is showing more and more.

Jinx just needs a home with loads of patience and love, and people who will understand trust is going to a long time.I can’t wait to see Jinx blossom more and more each day.

Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder.He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. Despite his trust issues, he has allowed a small amount of fuss, although he remains very wary and unsure of our intentions. He will need lots of time, patience and gentle handling while he learns that he is safe.Because of this, Jinx will need another kind and confident dog in his new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for him as he begins to settle and gain some confidence.We have not yet cat tested Jinx, but given what we have seen from him so far, it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. He will need a quiet, experienced home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be very patient with him.Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He is a very scared boy and may need to be muzzled for formal handling eg. vet visits.Jinx has arrived with a sore eye, so we are keeping on top of cleaning it and making sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.Jinx has a long way to go, but the fact that he has already allowed a little fuss shows that there is a gentle side beneath all those worries. We hope that with the right canine companion, experienced adopters and lots of patience, he will slowly learn to trust and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.
